issues.fix: Download to a file, verify a checksum / signature, then execute.

Fast confirmation check for up to 100 Solana transaction signatures in one call (getSignatureStatuses with history search): found or not, processed / confirmed / finalized, success or the on-chain error, slot and confirmations, plus counts. Built for agents polling payments or swaps they just sent. Public Solana RPC, read-only.

signatures.description: Transaction signatures (base58), comma list or JSON array, max 100

searchHistory.description: Also search older ledger history (not only the recent status cache)

exampleOutput.note: not_found means the signature is unknown to this RPC: never sent, dropped, expired blockhash, or (with searchHistory=false) older than the status cache.

endpoints.description: Solana validator set from getVoteAccounts: active and delinquent counts, total active stake, Nakamoto coefficient (fewest validators controlling > 33.3% of stake), the top validators by stake with commission, stake %, last vote, root slot and last-epoch vote credits, or one validator by vote or identity key. Cached 5 minutes. Public Solana RPC, read-only.

limit.description: Top validators by stake to list

validator.description: Look up one validator by vote account or identity (node) pubkey

endpoints.description: Offline validator and chain detector for up to 50 crypto addresses: EVM (EIP-55 checksum, returns the checksummed form), Bitcoin (P2PKH, P2SH, SegWit v0 bech32, Taproot bech32m, testnet), Solana (32-byte base58, wallet vs program-derived/off-curve), Tron, XRP, Litecoin, Dogecoin, Dash and Cosmos-SDK bech32 chains. Catches typos via checksums before an agent sends funds. No network calls.

addresses.description: Addresses to check, comma list or JSON array, max 50

chain.description: Expected chain; addresses valid only for another chain are reported invalid with the detected chain

results.type: on-curve public key (wallet, mint or program keypair)

endpoints.description: Exact (string-math, no floating point) conversion between human token amounts and on-chain base units: wei / gwei / ether, lamports / SOL, sats / BTC, USDC/USDT (6 decimals) or any token with a decimals value. Returns the converted amount, the integer base units (decimal and hex) and every unit of the family. Accepts decimals, scientific notation and 0x-hex raw amounts.

from.description: Unit of amount (raw = integer base units)

decimals.description: Token decimals, needed for unit "token" (and for raw <-> token)

endpoints.description: Build EVM calldata offline: function selector + ABI-encoded arguments from a human signature such as transfer(address,uint256) or exactInputSingle((address,address,uint24,address,uint256,uint256,uint160)). Tuples/structs, fixed and dynamic arrays, bytes, strings and signed ints supported. mode=params gives abi.encode without a selector, mode=packed gives abi.encodePacked plus its keccak256 (as used for hashes and signatures). Returns hex, 32-byte words and length.

signature.description: Function signature, e.g. transfer(address,uint256); param names allowed; for mode=params/packed just the type list, e.g. (address,uint256)

args.description: Arguments as a JSON array (nested arrays for arrays/tuples; big integers as strings; bytes as 0x-hex)

mode.description: call = selector + abi.encode, params = abi.encode only, packed = abi.encodePacked

endpoints.description: Predict EVM contract addresses before deployment: CREATE (deployer + nonce, RLP-encoded; up to 50 consecutive nonces) or CREATE2 (deployer + salt + init code or its keccak256 hash, EIP-1014). Works for every EVM chain; returns EIP-55 checksummed addresses. No network calls.

nonce.description: CREATE: account nonce of the deployer (contracts start at 1)

count.description: CREATE: how many consecutive nonces to list

initCodeHash.description: CREATE2: keccak256 of the init code (0x + 64 hex)

initCode.description: CREATE2: init code hex (alternative to initCodeHash, max ~1.9 KB in a URL)

exampleOutput.note: EOAs start at nonce 0; contract deployers (factories) start at nonce 1 (EIP-161).

endpoints.description: Verify an Ethereum signature offline: recovers the signer address (secp256k1 ecrecover) from an EIP-191 personal_sign message (UTF-8 or hex) or a raw 32-byte digest (e.g. an EIP-712 hash), compares it with an expected address, flags malleable high-s signatures, accepts 65-byte r,s,v and 64-byte EIP-2098 compact signatures, and parses Sign-In with Ethereum (EIP-4361) messages (domain, nonce, chain, expiry). For smart-contract wallets (EIP-1271) recovery does not apply.

signature.description: 0x signature: 65 bytes r,s,v or 64 bytes EIP-2098

message.description: Signed message for personal_sign (EIP-191); give message or hash

messageEncoding.description: How to read message: UTF-8 text or 0x-hex bytes

hash.description: Raw 32-byte digest that was signed (no prefix added), e.g. an EIP-712 digest

address.description: Expected signer, to get match true/false

exampleOutput.note: Valid for EOAs. Smart-contract wallets (Safe, ERC-4337) sign via EIP-1271 and need an on-chain isValidSignature call.

endpoints.description: EIP-712 typed-data hashing and signature check: returns encodeType, typeHash, domain separator, struct hash and the final digest a wallet signs (eth_signTypedData_v4), and with a signature recovers the signer and compares it to an expected address. Summarises common payloads (ERC-2612 Permit, EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization used by x402 EVM payments, Permit2) so an agent can see what it is about to sign. POST JSON body.

typedData.description: The eth_signTypedData_v4 payload: {types, primaryType, domain, message} (EIP712Domain type optional, inferred from domain keys)

signature.description: Optional 65-byte or 64-byte signature to recover the signer

exampleOutput.encodeType: Mail(Person from,Person to,string contents)Person(string name,address wallet)

endpoints.description: Derive Solana program-derived addresses offline: findProgramAddress (canonical bump search) for any program and typed seeds (utf8, base58 pubkey, hex, u8/u16/u32/u64 little- or big-endian), or the associated token account (ATA) of an owner + mint for SPL Token or Token-2022. Same algorithm as @solana/web3.js (sha256 + ed25519 off-curve check). Useful to locate token accounts, Anchor PDAs and vaults without an RPC.

preset.description: ata = associated token account of owner + mint; custom = programId + seeds

seeds.description: custom: seeds as "utf8:vault", "pubkey:<base58>", "hex:0a0b", "u8:1", "u64:42", "u32be:7" (no prefix: a 32-byte base58 string is a pubkey, else utf8); JSON array if a seed contains commas

bump.description: custom: use this bump (createProgramAddress) instead of searching

owner.description: ata: wallet that owns the token account

endpoints.description: Impermanent loss calculator for AMM liquidity positions: full-range constant-product pools (Uniswap v2, Raydium, Orca classic) or concentrated ranges (Uniswap v3/v4, Orca Whirlpools, Raydium CLMM, Meteora) from entry price, current price and an optional price range. Returns LP value vs simply holding, the loss in percent and money, token amounts at entry and now, in-range status and, with a fee APR, the fees earned and break-even.

entryPrice.description: Price of token0 in token1 (e.g. ETH in USDC) when the position was opened

depositValue.description: Position value at entry, in token1 / quote terms

rangeLower.description: Concentrated liquidity: lower price bound (omit both bounds for full range)

feeApr.description: Optional pool fee APR in percent, to estimate fees earned

days.description: Days the position has been / will be open (for fees)

fees.note: simple (non-compounded) fee estimate on the entry value; real fees depend on volume and time in range

endpoints.description: Liquidation calculator. mode=perp: isolated-margin long/short liquidation and bankruptcy price from entry price, leverage and maintenance margin rate (optionally size and fees), with distance to liquidation. mode=lending: health factor, liquidation price of the collateral and safe borrow headroom for Aave/Compound/Kamino/Morpho-style loans from collateral, debt and liquidation threshold.

maintenanceMarginPct.description: perp: maintenance margin rate in percent

size.description: perp: optional position size in base units (for margin and notional)

feePct.description: perp: optional closing fee in percent of notional, reserved from margin

currentPrice.description: Optional current price for distance and status (default entryPrice / collateralPrice)

debt.description: lending: debt value in the same quote currency

exampleOutput.note: isolated margin, linear (USD-margined) contract; exchanges add tiered maintenance rates and funding, so treat as an estimate

endpoints.description: Risk-based position sizing for trading agents: from account balance, risk per trade (percent or fixed amount), entry and stop price returns units to buy/sell, notional, leverage needed, stop distance, and with a target the reward:risk ratio, profit at target and break-even win rate. Optional fees and lot-size rounding.

riskPct.description: Percent of the account to risk

stopPrice.description: Stop loss; below entry = long, above = short

feePct.description: Fee per side in percent of notional (included in the risk)

lotSize.description: Round units down to this step (e.g. 0.001 BTC, 1 share)

endpoints.description: Loan / mortgage amortization: periodic payment, total interest, payoff date and a yearly or full payment schedule (principal, interest, balance) for any rate, term and payment frequency (monthly, bi-weekly, weekly, quarterly, annual). Extra payments per period show months and interest saved. Fixed-rate, level-payment loans.

annualRatePct.description: Nominal annual interest rate in percent

startDate.description: First payment date YYYY-MM-DD (for payoff date)

schedule.description: Schedule detail (full is capped at 600 rows)

endpoints.description: Investment appraisal for a cash-flow series: NPV at a discount rate, IRR (all roots for non-conventional flows), MIRR, profitability index, simple and discounted payback; with dates gives Excel-compatible XNPV and XIRR. POST JSON body {cashFlows, ratePct, dates?}.

cashFlows.description: Cash flows per period starting at t=0 (investments negative)

ratePct.description: Discount rate per period (or per year with dates), percent

dates.description: Optional YYYY-MM-DD date per cash flow for XNPV / XIRR (Actual/365)

endpoints.description: Compound growth / savings calculator: future value of a principal plus monthly contributions at any compounding frequency (incl. continuous), contributions at start or end of month, inflation-adjusted value, APR <-> APY conversion, doubling time, months to reach a target and a yearly breakdown. Works for savings, staking yields and DCA projections.

annualRatePct.description: Nominal annual rate (APR) in percent; or give apyPct

apyPct.description: Effective annual yield in percent (converted to the APR for the compounding)

inflationPct.description: Annual inflation for the real (today's money) value

target.description: Optional goal amount: months needed to reach it

endpoints.description: European option pricing (Black-Scholes-Merton with continuous dividend yield): call and put prices, delta, gamma, vega, theta per day, rho, d1/d2 and probability of finishing in the money; with a market price it solves implied volatility. Works for equity, index and crypto options (set the yield to 0).

volatilityPct.description: Annualised volatility in percent (not needed when solving implied vol)

marketPrice.description: Option market price: solve implied volatility (needs type call or put)

endpoints.description: Fixed-coupon bond math: price from yield or yield to maturity from price (clean and dirty, with accrued interest for fractional periods), current yield, Macaulay and modified duration, convexity and DV01, plus the cash-flow schedule. Treasury, corporate or zero-coupon bonds; any coupon frequency.

couponRatePct.description: Annual coupon rate in percent (0 = zero-coupon)

ytmPct.description: Yield to maturity in percent: compute price

price.description: Clean price (same units as faceValue): compute yield

exampleOutput.note: yield is compounded at the coupon frequency (bond-equivalent); price per faceValue

endpoints.description: Technical analysis on a price series you supply: SMA, EMA, RSI (Wilder), MACD (line, signal, histogram), Bollinger Bands (%B, bandwidth), ATR, Stochastic %K/%D, OBV, VWAP and rate of change, with latest values, optional recent series and plain signals (overbought/oversold, MACD cross, trend vs moving average). Closes only, or OHLCV candles. POST JSON body.

close.description: Closing prices, oldest first (or give candles)

candles.description: OHLCV candles oldest first: objects {open,high,low,close,volume} or arrays [time,open,high,low,close,volume]

indicators.description: Which indicators (atr, stochastic, obv, vwap need candles)

series.description: Also return the last N values of each indicator

endpoints.description: Portfolio and asset risk/return analytics from price or return series you supply: annualised return (CAGR) and volatility, Sharpe and Sortino ratios, max drawdown, historical and parametric 95% VaR, beta/alpha against a benchmark series and a correlation matrix, for each asset and the weighted (periodically rebalanced) portfolio. Up to 20 assets. POST JSON body.

returns.description: Alternatively periodic simple returns per asset as decimals (0.01 = 1%)

weights.description: Portfolio weights per asset (normalised; default equal)

benchmark.description: Name of the series to use as benchmark for beta/alpha (excluded from the portfolio unless weighted)

periodsPerYear.description: 252 trading days, 365 crypto days, 52 weeks, 12 months

exampleOutput.note: simple returns, portfolio rebalanced every period; VaR is a one-period loss at 95% confidence

endpoints.description: How much house can I afford: maximum home price and loan from income, monthly debts, down payment and rate under front-end / back-end debt-to-income limits (default 28/36), with a full monthly PITI breakdown (principal & interest, property tax, insurance, HOA, PMI below 20% down). Give homePrice instead to get the monthly cost and the income needed.

monthlyDebts.description: Other monthly debt payments (cards, car, student loans)

propertyTaxPct.description: Annual property tax, percent of price

pmiPct.description: Annual PMI, percent of loan, when down payment < 20%

homePrice.description: Optional: evaluate this price instead of solving for the maximum

exampleOutput.note: estimate only; lenders also weigh credit score, reserves and local taxes/insurance

endpoints.description: SaaS / subscription unit economics: customer lifetime value (margin-adjusted), LTV:CAC ratio, CAC payback months, average lifetime, MRR/ARR, break-even customer count and cash runway, with health ratings against common benchmarks (LTV:CAC >= 3, payback <= 12 months). For startups, API businesses and agent services.

arpuMonthly.description: Average revenue per customer per month

cashBalance.description: Cash in the bank, for runway

discountRatePct.description: Optional annual discount rate for a discounted LTV

endpoints.description: Depreciation schedules: straight-line, declining balance (any factor, optional switch to straight-line), double-declining, sum-of-the-years-digits and US MACRS GDS (3/5/7/10/15/20-year, half-year convention, computed from the IRS rules: 200% or 150% DB switching to straight-line). Year-by-year depreciation, accumulated depreciation and book value.

lifeYears.description: Useful life; for MACRS the recovery class 3, 5, 7, 10, 15 or 20

switchToStraightLine.description: Declining balance: switch to straight-line when it gives more

endpoints.description: Structural diff of two JSON documents: list of added / removed / changed values with JSON Pointer paths and old/new values, an RFC 6902 JSON Patch that turns a into b, and counts. Arrays are aligned by longest common subsequence (inserted items show as inserts, not a cascade of changes) or matched by an id field. POST JSON body {a, b}.

arrayKey.description: Match array elements that are objects by this field (e.g. "id") instead of by position

endpoints.description: Apply a JSON Patch (RFC 6902: add, remove, replace, move, copy, test) or a JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7386) to a JSON document and return the result. Atomic: any failing operation or test returns 422 with the operation index and nothing is applied. POST JSON body {document, patch}.

patch.description: RFC 6902 operations array, or an object = RFC 7386 merge patch

endpoints.description: Query JSON with JSONPath (RFC 9535): dot and bracket names, indexes, slices, wildcards, recursive descent (..) and filters with comparisons, && || !, and length() / count() / match() / search() / value() functions, e.g. $.store.book[?@.price < 10].title. Returns matched values with their normalized paths. Several queries per call. POST JSON body {json, query}.

queries.description: Several expressions at once (alternative to query)

endpoints.description: Infer a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) from one JSON document or many samples: types (integer vs number), nested objects and arrays, required keys (present in every sample), nullable fields, string formats (date-time, date, email, uri, uuid, ipv4/6) and optionally enums and numeric bounds. Turns API responses into a contract for validation or tool definitions. POST JSON body.

samples.description: Several sample documents of the same shape (better required/nullable detection)

enums.description: Emit enum for low-cardinality repeated strings

endpoints.description: Generate typed models from sample JSON: TypeScript interfaces, Zod schemas, Python Pydantic models, Go structs (json tags) or Rust serde structs. Nested objects become named types, optional and nullable fields are detected across samples, arrays are typed by their merged items. POST JSON body {json or samples, language, rootName}.

Profile a CSV/TSV dataset: delimiter detection, row and column counts, per-column inferred type (integer, decimal, boolean, date, datetime, string), null/empty counts, distinct values, min/max/mean/median/std and percentiles for numbers, length stats and detected patterns (email, URL, phone) for text, top values, duplicate rows and data-quality warnings. Up to 50,000 rows. POST JSON body {csv}.

Turn CSV/TSV into SQL: CREATE TABLE with inferred column types (integer/bigint, numeric, boolean, date, timestamp, varchar/text, NOT NULL where never empty, optional primary key) and batched INSERT statements with correct quoting and escaping for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite or SQL Server. Up to 20,000 rows. POST JSON body {csv, table, dialect}.

endpoints.description: Format and lint SQL: consistent keyword case, one clause per line, indented select lists, joins, AND/OR conditions and subqueries, comments and string literals preserved; or minify. The linter flags UPDATE/DELETE without WHERE, SELECT *, implicit comma joins, leading-wildcard LIKE, ORDER BY RAND(), NOT IN with subqueries and string-concatenation injection smells, and lists statement types and referenced tables. POST JSON body {sql}.

endpoints.description: Run XPath 1.0 queries over XML you supply (RSS/Atom, SOAP, sitemaps, SVG, config) or over HTML for scraping: returns matched elements/attributes/text with their paths, text, attributes and outer markup, or the number/string/boolean result of an expression. endpoints.description: Semantic versioning toolkit with npm (node-semver) semantics: validate and parse a version, compare two versions, test a range (^, ~, x-ranges, hyphen ranges, || unions, prerelease rules) and show its comparator form, sort a list and pick the max/min version satisfying a range, and bump (major, minor, patch, pre*, prerelease with an identifier).

versions.description: Versions to sort / filter by range

endpoints.description: IPv4 / IPv6 subnet calculator: network and broadcast/last address, netmask, wildcard, first/last usable host, address and host counts, address type (private, CGNAT, documentation, ULA, link-local...), reverse-DNS zone, expanded/compressed IPv6; check whether IPs fall inside, and split the block into smaller subnets. endpoints.description: Unit conversion across 14 categories with exact defined factors: length, mass, volume (US and imperial), area, speed, time, data (SI kB vs IEC KiB, bits vs bytes), pressure, energy, power, angle, frequency, temperature (C, F, K, Rankine) and fuel economy (mpg US/UK, L/100 km, km/L). all.description: Also return the value in every unit of the category

endpoints.description: Convert a colour between HEX, RGB(A), HSL, HSV, CMYK, CIE Lab and OKLCH (any CSS colour syntax or one of the 148 CSS names in), with relative luminance, contrast against white and black, the readable text colour and the nearest CSS named colour (CIE76 delta-E). on: pull_request_target
jobs:
  greet:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - run: echo "${{ github.event.pull_request.title }}"

findings.message: checkout of untrusted PR code (${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}) in a privileged workflow: any later build/install step runs attacker code with secrets and a write token

findings.message: some-org/labeler@main tracks a moving branch: any push to it runs in your workflow

endpoints.description: Evaluate math expressions safely and exactly — the calculator agents should call instead of doing arithmetic in their heads. Exact rational arithmetic by default (0.1 + 0.2 = 3/10, 1/3 + 1/6 = 1/2, 2^200 and 1000! in full), with repeating-decimal notation, plus floating point for transcendental functions: sqrt, cbrt, root, exp, ln, log (base 10, or log(x, b)), log2, trig and hyperbolic functions (radians or degrees), gamma, erf, factorial, nCr / nPr, gcd / lcm, mod, min / max / sum / mean / median, round(x, digits), comparisons. Implicit multiplication (2pi, 3(x+1)), variables, and multi-statement scripts ("r = 2; pi r^2"). No code execution.

expr.description: Expression, or statements separated by ";" (assign with name = expr; the last value is returned)

vars.description: Variables, e.g. "x=2, rate=0.05" or a JSON object

mode.description: auto: exact rationals whenever possible; float: IEEE double throughout

endpoints.description: Solve equations exactly where possible. Polynomials of any degree up to 100: exact rational roots, exact surd forms for quadratic factors ("(3 + √5)/2", complex "(-1 + i√3)/2"), multiplicities via square-free factorisation, and high-precision numeric roots (Aberth–Ehrlich + Newton polishing) for the rest. Any other single-variable equation ("cos(x) = x", "2^x = x^2 + 1", "ln(x) + x = 5") is solved numerically over a range with sign scanning + Brent's method, rejecting poles. Systems of linear equations ("2x + 3y = 7", "x - y = 1") are solved with exact rational Gaussian elimination, reporting unique, none, or infinitely many solutions in parametric form.

Linear algebra on matrices, exactly where it matters. Determinant, inverse, RREF, rank, null space, linear solve (Ax = b), multiply, add / subtract, integer powers, trace and LU are computed with exact rational arithmetic (entries may be integers, decimals or "p/q" strings — 0.1 stays 1/10), returned as exact values plus decimals. Floating-point eigenvalues (Jacobi for symmetric matrices with eigenvectors; Hessenberg + shifted QR for general matrices including complex eigenvalues, with eigenvectors for real eigenvalues), singular values (one-sided Jacobi SVD), QR, norms and condition number. op=analyze returns determinant, rank, trace, inverse, symmetry and eigenvalues in one call.

a.description: Matrix A as an array of rows (max 40x40; 30x30 for exact ops). Entries: numbers or "p/q" strings

b.description: Matrix B (multiply / add / subtract) or right-hand side vector / matrix (solve)

Several named series also get Pearson and Spearman correlation matrices. Accepts numbers, numeric strings, nulls / "NA" (missing) or objects plus a field name.

endpoints.description: Fit a regression model and get the full statistical table, like R's summary(lm) or statsmodels. Linear, polynomial (degree 2–6), exponential (y = a·e^(bx)), logarithmic, power (y = a·x^b), multiple linear (many named predictors) and binary logistic regression (IRLS, odds ratios, McFadden pseudo-R², accuracy). Returns coefficients with standard errors, t / z statistics, p-values and confidence intervals, R² and adjusted R², residual standard error, F-test, AIC / BIC, a residual summary, the fitted equation, and predictions with confidence and prediction intervals. model=best ranks the single-predictor models by adjusted R² on the original scale. Numerically stable Householder QR.

endpoints.description: Run a statistical significance test and get the statistic, p-value, effect size, confidence interval and a plain-English verdict — results match scipy.stats. Tests: Welch / Student two-sample t, paired t, one-sample t, one-proportion z, A/B test of two conversion rates (pooled z, lift, CI of the difference), chi-square goodness of fit and independence (Yates for 2×2, Cramér's V), one-way ANOVA (η²), Kruskal–Wallis, Mann–Whitney U (exact for small samples, rank-biserial r), Wilcoxon signed-rank (exact / permutation / normal), Pearson and Spearman correlation (Fisher-z CI) and Fisher's exact test. Two-sided or one-sided alternatives.

endpoints.description: Provably fair random draws for giveaways, raffles, games and A/B assignment. endpoints.description: Convert public keys between PEM, JWK and OpenSSH formats and compute their identifiers — what an agent needs to publish a JWKS, configure an OIDC / JWT verifier or pin a key. Accepts SPKI or PKCS#1 PEM, X.509 certificates (PEM or base64 DER), OpenSSH public keys, a JWK or a whole JWKS. Returns the public JWK (RSA, EC P-256 / P-384 / P-521 / secp256k1, OKP Ed25519 / Ed448 / X25519 / X448), RFC 7638 thumbprint (and RFC 9278 thumbprint URI), SPKI PEM, OpenSSH line with its SHA256 fingerprint, the pin-sha256 SPKI hash, x5t / x5t#S256 for certificates, suggested JWS algorithms and weak-key warnings. Public keys only: private keys are refused, never processed.

endpoints.description: Create or verify HMAC-signed JWTs (HS256 / HS384 / HS512) — for test fixtures, service-to-service tokens, webhook auth and debugging "invalid signature" errors. sign: builds header + claims with iat / exp / nbf from durations ("15m", "1h", "7d"), iss / sub / aud shortcuts and an optional random jti, and returns the compact token. verify: checks the signature in constant time plus exp / nbf / iat with leeway and optional issuer / audience expectations, and explains exactly why a token fails. The secret can be UTF-8, base64, base64url or hex; it is never echoed or stored. Warns when the secret is shorter than the hash (RFC 7518 §3.2). For RS / ES / EdDSA token decoding and JWKS verification use /v1/jwt-decode.

endpoints.description: Hash, verify and identify password hashes — for seeding users, migrating auth systems, writing htpasswd files and auditing leaked hash formats. hash: bcrypt, Argon2id / Argon2i (where the server has libargon2), PBKDF2-SHA256 / SHA512 (Django format), SHA-512 / SHA-256 crypt (Linux shadow) and Apache APR1 (htpasswd). verify: checks a password against bcrypt, Argon2, crypt ($1$ $5$ $6$, DES), APR1, Django / Werkzeug / passlib PBKDF2, phpass ($P$ $H$, WordPress), Drupal 7 ($S$), LDAP {SSHA} / {SHA} / {SSHA256} / {SSHA512} / {SMD5}, MySQL 4.1+ and unsalted MD5 / SHA / NTLM hex. identify: algorithm, parameters and a verdict against the OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet, with needsRehash. endpoints.description: Decode and inspect SAML 2.0 messages for SSO debugging: paste a SAMLResponse / SAMLRequest (base64 from an HTTP-POST form, deflated + URL-encoded from an HTTP-Redirect URL, the whole redirect URL, or raw XML) or IdP / SP metadata. Returns the message type, issuer, destination, status, every assertion (NameID and format, subject confirmation, conditions with NotBefore / NotOnOrAfter checked against now, audiences, AuthnContext, session index, attributes), signature placement and algorithms, embedded certificates (subject, expiry, SHA-256 fingerprint) and metadata endpoints. Flags unsigned responses, SHA-1, signature references that do not cover their parent (XML Signature Wrapping), multiple assertions, comments inside NameID, expired conditions and expired certificates. DTDs are rejected (XXE-safe); signatures are inspected, not cryptographically verified.

endpoints.description: Parse DMARC aggregate (RUA) reports and SMTP TLS reports (TLS-RPT, RFC 8460) into an actionable summary. TLS-RPT: per-policy success / failure counts and failure details. No DNS or network lookups.

exampleOutput.note: Self-signatures are read but not cryptographically verified.

endpoints.description: Look up TLS cipher suites by IANA name, OpenSSL name, GnuTLS name or hex code (0x13,0x01 / 0xC02F) — one or a whole list from a scanner, server config or ClientHello — and get key exchange, authentication, cipher, MAC / PRF hash, AEAD and forward-secrecy flags, minimum protocol, the IANA Recommended flag (Y / N / Discouraged) and a security rating (recommended, secure, weak, insecure) with reasons: no forward secrecy, CBC, SHA-1, RC4, 3DES, EXPORT, NULL or anonymous. Lists get a summary and their worst suite. Without a suite, browse the 356-entry IANA registry filtered by protocol or rating. Offline data: IANA registry, OpenSSL 3.6 and GnuTLS names.

suite.description: One or more suites (names or hex), separated by spaces, colons, commas or newlines

exampleOutput.verdict: Disable the weak suites (no forward secrecy, CBC or SHA-1) unless you must support very old clients.

reasons: no forward secrecy (static RSA key exchange)
CBC mode (padding-oracle attacks such as Lucky13)

endpoints.description: Money formatting and math with CLDR data (ICU 78 / CLDR 48, matches Intl.NumberFormat): format an amount for any of 60 locales and 154 active ISO 4217 currencies (symbol, narrow symbol or code; standard or accounting negatives; Indian lakh grouping, Swiss apostrophes, RTL marks), round with 9 modes or cash rounding (CHF 0.05), parse a formatted string such as "1.234,56 €" or "(US$1,234.50)" back to an exact amount and currency, split an amount by ratios without losing a cent (largest remainder) and look up currency or country info (digits, symbols, cash rounding, countries). Exact decimal arithmetic, no floats.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code (default: the locale's country currency)

country.description: ISO 3166 country: use its currency (info: list it)

locale.description: en-US, de-DE, fr-CH, ja-JP, hi-IN ... or just a language

endpoints.description: Day-count conventions and accrued interest for bonds, loans and swaps: days and year fraction between two dates under ACT/360, ACT/365F, ACT/ACT ISDA, NL/365, 30/360 (ISDA bond basis), 30/360 US (SIA end-of-February rules), 30E/360 and 30E/360 ISDA, with simple interest on a principal; or, for a fixed-coupon bond, the coupon schedule around a settlement date (previous / next coupon, end-of-month rule), accrued days and accrued interest per face amount, including ACT/ACT ICMA (Treasuries). Matches QuantLib.

ratePct.description: between: annual simple rate for the interest amount; coupon: coupon rate

maturity.description: coupon: maturity date; between: termination date for 30E/360 ISDA

notes: 30/360 = ISDA 2006 4.16(f) bond basis; 30/360-US adds the SIA end-of-February rules; 30E/360-ISDA treats February month-end as day 30 except a February maturity (pass maturity).

endpoints.description: True cost of a loan including fees: the US Truth in Lending APR (Regulation Z actuarial method) and the EU APRC (Consumer Credit Directive annual effective rate), plus the payment, amount financed, finance charge and total of payments for a level-payment loan. Handles origination fees and points paid upfront or rolled into the loan, a balloon payment, and weekly to annual payments. Compares the note rate with the real borrowing rate so offers can be ranked.

fees.description: Prepaid finance charges (origination, points, broker fees)

points.description: Discount points as % of the loan amount (added to fees)

feesFinanced.description: true: fees are added to the loan balance; false: paid upfront / deducted from proceeds

balloon.description: Extra amount due with the last payment

payment.description: Use this payment instead of computing it

notes: APR (US Reg Z, actuarial): periodic IRR of amount financed vs payments × payments per year. APRC (EU CCD): (1 + periodic IRR)^payments per year − 1, equal periods.
Payments are rounded to cents with interest rounded each period; the final payment absorbs the rounding difference.

endpoints.description: Payment card number checks without storing anything: Luhn checksum, brand / network from the IIN (Visa, Mastercard incl. 2-series, Amex, Discover, Diners, JCB, UnionPay, Maestro, Mir, Elo, Hipercard, Verve, RuPay, Dankort, Troy, UATP), allowed lengths, CVV length, card-number spacing, known public test numbers (Stripe, Braintree, Adyen) and expiry validity. Returns only the PCI-safe first 6 / last 4 — never the full number. Up to 100 numbers per call. POST so numbers stay out of URLs and logs.

exampleOutput.note: Only first 6 / last 4 digits are returned; nothing is stored. A valid number says nothing about funds or whether the card exists.

endpoints.description: Validate bank routing identifiers offline (IBAN is covered by /v1/iban-validate): US ABA routing numbers (3-7-1 checksum, Federal Reserve district, thrift / electronic ranges), SWIFT / BIC (bank, ISO country, location, branch, test and passive BICs), Mexican CLABE (checksum, bank, plaza), Argentine CBU (both check digits), Canadian routing numbers (EFT 0YYYXXXXX and MICR XXXXX-YYY, institution names), UK sort codes, Australian BSB (bank and state) and Indian IFSC (bank). Auto-detects the type from the format.

Credit-card and revolving-balance payoff in exact cents. Give a balance, an annual percentage rate, and a fixed payment (or a minimum that is the greater of a percent of the new balance and a floor). Returns the months to zero, total interest, total paid, and a yearly rollup. Interest each month is round-half-up of balance × APR / 12. The last payment is the remaining balance plus that month's interest. Refuses a payment that does not cover the interest.

minPercent.description: Instead of a fixed payment: percent of the new balance (after interest)

minFloor.description: Minimum payment floor used with minPercent, default 0

start.description: First payment date YYYY-MM-DD. Later payments fall on the same day, clamped to the month end

exampleOutput.method: Monthly interest is balance × APR / 12, rounded half away from zero to the cent. The last payment is the remaining balance plus that month's interest.

endpoints.description: Invoice math in exact cents. Each line is quantity × unit price, then an optional line discount, rounded half away from zero to the cent. An invoice-level discount comes off the subtotal, then tax is that percent of the discounted subtotal, rounded the same way. Returns every line, the subtotal, discount, tax, and total. A discount larger than the amount it applies to is rejected.

lines.description: Each line: qty, unitPrice, optional description and discountPct

discountPct.description: Invoice discount percent off the subtotal, default 0

discountAmount.description: Invoice discount as money, instead of discountPct

taxPct.description: Tax percent of the discounted subtotal, default 0

exampleOutput.method: Each line is quantity × unit price, minus the line discount, rounded half away from zero to the cent. Tax is the invoice discount applied to that subtotal, then the tax percent, rounded the same way.

endpoints.description: Gross pay in exact cents. Hourly: regular hours at the rate, overtime hours at a multiplier (default 1.5) and double-time hours at a multiplier (default 2). Weekly: hours above the threshold (default 40) are overtime. Salary: the annual amount is split across 52, 26, 24 or 12 periods so the paychecks add back to the annual amount. Extra straight-time hours are paid at annual / 2080 (52 × 40). Overtime and double-time hours use that same base rate times their multipliers.

rate.description: Hourly rate, or the annual salary in salary mode

hours.description: Hours worked (weekly mode, or extra hours on top of a salary)

weeklyThreshold.description: Weekly mode: hours before overtime, default 40

exampleOutput.note: Hours above the weekly threshold are overtime. Each piece is rounded half away from zero to the cent.

endpoints.description: Prorate a money amount across a date range, in exact cents. The window is half-open: from the start date up to but not including the end date. The charge is amount × days used / days in the period, rounded half away from zero. The used range has to sit inside the period.

exampleOutput.method: Half-open dates, [start, end). Share = amount × used days / period days, rounded half away from zero to the cent.

endpoints.description: Price, margin and markup in exact cents. Analyze a cost and a price (margin is profit / price, markup is profit / cost). Or set a price from a cost and a margin percent (price = cost / (1 − margin)), or from a markup percent (price = cost × (1 + markup)). Or walk a list of successive discounts off a price, rounding each step half away from zero to the cent.

exampleOutput.method: Margin = profit / price. Markup = profit / cost. A price from a margin is cost / (1 − margin). Percents are rounded half away from zero to 4 decimal places.

endpoints.description: Width of one line in Helvetica or Helvetica-Bold, in points. Glyph widths are the Adobe standard-14 AFM numbers in WinAnsi (the same numbers ReportLab ships). The width is the sum times the font size, rounded half away from zero to 0.001 pt. Characters outside that encoding, and control characters, are rejected. A newline belongs in text-wrap.

exampleOutput.method: Adobe AFM WinAnsi widths × font size, rounded half away from zero to 0.001 pt.

endpoints.description: Wrap text to a measure in Helvetica or Helvetica-Bold. Hard breaks are LF, CR, or CRLF. Inside a paragraph, spaces collapse to one and leading and trailing spaces are dropped. A word moves to the next line when it does not fit. A word wider than the whole measure breaks between characters, and those lines are marked broken. The width of each line uses the same AFM rounding as text-width.

exampleOutput.method: Greedy wrap on spaces. A word wider than the measure breaks between characters. Line widths are AFM millipoints.

endpoints.description: Cut one Helvetica line so it fits a width, ending with an ellipsis (…) when the text is too long. The ellipsis is the WinAnsi character. If the whole line already fits, it is returned unchanged. If even the ellipsis is wider than the measure, the call is rejected.

Largest Helvetica size, on a fixed step, at which one line still fits a width. Sizes run from minSize to maxSize in steps (defaults 6, 72 and 0.5 points). Empty text fits at maxSize. If the line does not fit at minSize, the call is rejected. Width uses the same AFM rounding as text-width, so the size is not a float division of the two widths.

Wrap a Helvetica block and give its height. Line breaking is the same as text-wrap. Leading defaults to 1.2 times the font size, rounded half away from zero to 0.001 pt. Block height is the line count times the leading, and a blank line from a hard break counts. An empty string has height zero.

leading.description: Line height in points. Default is 1.2 × size

exampleOutput.method: Block height = line count × leading. Default leading is 1.2 × the font size, rounded half away from zero to 0.001 pt.

endpoints.description: ISBN-10 and ISBN-13 check digit. Spaces and hyphens are ignored, and a 9-digit number is read as an ISBN-10 with a leading zero. ISBN-13 must use the 978 or 979 prefix. A valid ISBN-10 is also returned as ISBN-13, and a 978 ISBN-13 is also returned as ISBN-10. This does not check that the publisher prefix was ever assigned.
ISSN check digit (8 characters, the last may be X). Spaces and hyphens are ignored. The formatted form is the two groups of four.

IMEI and IMEISV. A 15-digit IMEI must pass the Luhn check. A 14-digit IMEI has no check digit, and a 16-digit IMEISV has none either. Spaces and hyphens are ignored. This does not look the number up with a manufacturer.

GTIN check digit for EAN-8, UPC-A (12 digits), EAN-13 and GTIN-14. The weight alternates 3 and 1 from the right, starting with 3 on the digit beside the check. Spaces and hyphens are ignored. This does not check that the GS1 prefix was assigned.

ISIN check digit (ISO 6166). Two letters, nine letters or digits, one check digit. Letters expand to their alphabet position (A = 10) and the Luhn sum of that digit string must be 0. The prefix must be an ISO country code or one of the substitute prefixes EU, QS, QT, XA, XB, XC, XD, XF, XK, XS. Spaces are ignored. The national security id inside is not looked up.

CUSIP check digit. Nine characters from digits, letters, and * @ #. Spaces are ignored and hyphens are not. From the left, values are weighted 1, 2, 1, 2 and the digits of those products sum to the check digit. A CUSIP made only of letters and digits is also returned as a US ISIN. This does not look the issuer up.

FIGI check digit. Twelve characters with no vowels. The first two are letters and are not BS, BM, GG, GB or VG, and the third character is G. The check uses the full A–Z alphabet, weights 1 and 2 from the left. Spaces are ignored. This does not call OpenFIGI.
LEI check digits, ISO 17442 with ISO 7064 mod 97-10. Twenty letters or digits, and the whole number is 1 mod 97. Spaces and hyphens are ignored. This does not look the entity up at GLEIF.

ISO 11649 creditor reference. RF, two check digits, then up to 21 letters or digits. Spaces, hyphens, dots, commas, slashes and colons are ignored. The check moves RF and the two digits to the end and requires ISO 7064 mod 97-10 to be 1. This does not look the creditor up.

ISO 6346 container check digit. Four letters (the fourth is U, J, Z or R), six serial digits and a check digit. Letter values skip every multiple of 11, then each value is multiplied by 2 to the power of its position. The total mod 11 mod 10 is the check digit. Spaces are ignored. This does not look the owner up at BIC.

CAS Registry Number check digit. Two to seven digits, a hyphen, two digits, a hyphen and a check digit. No leading zero. From the right, digits are weighted 1, 2, 3 and the total mod 10 is the check. A number typed without hyphens is split the same way. This does not look the substance up.

MEID, the CDMA equipment id. Hex is 14 digits with an optional Luhn check in base 16. Decimal is 18 digits (manufacturer and serial) with an optional decimal Luhn check, and it converts to the hex form. A 14-digit hex number that is only decimal digits is an IMEI, not a MEID. Spaces and hyphens are ignored.

IEC 60062 resistor color code. Decode 3 to 6 bands, or encode a resistance that lands exactly on a digit-and-multiplier value. Digits run black=0 through white=9. Multipliers run from silver (×0.01) and gold (×0.1) through white (×1e9). Tolerances: brown 1%, red 2%, green 0.5%, blue 0.25%, violet 0.1%, grey 0.05%, gold 5%, silver 10%. Three bands mean 20% and have no tolerance band. The sixth band is the temperature coefficient in ppm/K: black 250, brown 100, red 50, orange 15, yellow 25, green 20, blue 10, violet 5, grey 1. Grey may be spelled gray. This does not measure a part.

bands.description: Colors, commas or spaces. Omit to encode ohms instead.

ohms.description: Resistance to encode. Exact decimal or a fraction such as 47/10.

count.description: Bands when encoding. Default 4. Three bands are 20%.

tolerance.description: Percent when encoding: 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, or 20. Default 5% for 4 bands, 1% for 5 or 6, 20% for 3.

tempco.description: ppm/K. Required for 6 bands, and only then.

endpoints.description: Ohm's law for one passive resistor. Give any two of voltage (volts), current (amperes), resistance (ohms) and power (watts). The other two come back as exact rationals. A third or fourth value is checked and rejected when it disagrees. Zero volts across a positive resistance is a dead circuit. Voltage across zero ohms, or voltage with zero current, is rejected. Power and resistance are accepted only when both square roots are rational. SI units, no prefixes.

Unloaded voltage divider. r1 is the top resistor, from the supply to the output. r2 is the bottom resistor, from the output to ground. Returns the output voltage, the string current, and the power in each resistor as exact rationals. Both resistors must be positive. A zero supply gives zero output, zero current and zero power.

Series or parallel equivalent of 2 to 24 resistances. Series adds them. Parallel is the reciprocal of the sum of the reciprocals. Exact rationals. Every value must be positive. One block only: a mixed ladder is not a mode.

Series resistor for LEDs on one supply. Resistance is (supply − series × forward) / current, with volts and amperes. The part chosen is the next IEC 60063 E24 value at or above that resistance, so the LED current does not go over the request. The forward drop of the string must be under the supply. Exact rationals.

forward.description: Forward drop of one LED, volts

endpoints.description: Normalize a MAC-48 or EUI-64. Accepts colon, hyphen, Cisco dotted (groups of four) or plain hex, any case. Returns lowercase colon, hyphen, dotted and compact forms. multicast is the I/G bit, the low bit of the first octet. local is the U/L bit, the next bit. oui is the first three octets as hex, not a vendor name.

Modified EUI-64 from RFC 4291. A 48-bit MAC is expanded by flipping the U/L bit and inserting FF-FE in the middle. A 64-bit value with FF-FE in the middle is folded back to the MAC. Any other 64-bit value is returned as-is with mac null. The bits, local and multicast fields describe the 64-bit result. Flipping the bit makes a universal MAC look local in the interface id.

IPv6 address a host builds for itself from a /64 prefix and a MAC (SLAAC, RFC 4862). The interface id is the modified EUI-64. The prefix must be exactly 64 bits and the low 64 bits of the prefix must be zero. Also returns the link-local address and the solicited-node multicast address. Text is RFC 5952. No zone index and no IPv4 tail.

IPv6 solicited-node multicast address, ff02::1:ffXX:XXXX, from the low 24 bits of an IPv6 address or from the last three octets of a MAC. The U/L flip does not change those 24 bits, so the MAC and its SLAAC address share one solicited-node address. Hex groups only; no zone index.

A stable locally administered unicast MAC from a seed. SHA-256 of the seed, first six bytes, multicast bit cleared and the U/L bit set. The same seed always returns the same MAC. This is not a random draw and not a real assignment.

Convert one CSS absolute length. An inch is 96px and 2.54 cm, so a centimetre is 4800/127 px, a millimetre is 480/127 px, and Q (a quarter-millimetre) is 120/127 px. A point is 4/3 px and a pica is 16px. Units: px, in, cm, mm, Q, pt, pc. em, rem, percent and viewport units are rejected. Exact rationals, 12 decimal places.

Convert a CSS angle among deg, grad, turn and pirad. A degree is 1/360 turn, a gradian is 1/400 turn, and one pirad is π radians, which is half a turn. A raw radian value is rejected because π is not rational. Exact rationals.
Convert a CSS time between seconds and milliseconds. One millisecond is 1/1000 s. Minutes are not a CSS time unit. Exact rationals.
Convert a CSS resolution among dppx, dpi and dpcm. The alias x means dppx. One dppx is 96 dpi, and one inch is 2.54 cm, so one dpcm is 127/4800 dppx. Exact rationals.

Specificity of one CSS selector, from Selectors Level 4. a is IDs. b is classes, attributes and pseudo-classes. c is elements and pseudo-elements. :is(), :not() and :has() use only the most specific argument. :where() is zero. :nth-child() and :nth-last-child() are one pseudo-class, plus the most specific selector after of. :host() and :host-context() add one pseudo-class plus the argument. ::slotted() adds one pseudo-element plus the argument. ::part() is one pseudo-element. A comma list returns every selector; the top numbers are the most specific, the first on a tie. against compares those numbers. At most 50 selectors in a list. Backslashes and namespaces are rejected. A bad selector is an error, not dropped.

Explain a POSIX file mode. Accepts octal (755, 0755, 4755) or the 9-character ls form, with an optional leading type character. s and t mean the execute bit is also set; S and T mean the special bit without execute. setuid, setgid and sticky are the high octal digit. value is the mode as a decimal integer.

Apply a chmod mode to a starting mode. The grammar is GNU chmod: symbolic [ugoa]*([-+=][rwxXst]* or one of ugo), comma separated, or =644 / +1, or a bare octal. No spaces. If who is omitted, bits set in umask are not changed; the default umask is 0. Explicit who ignores umask. X adds execute only on a directory, or when an execute bit is already set. On a directory, bare octal shorter than five digits keeps set-user-ID and set-group-ID; =755, 00755, or a symbolic s clears them. The sticky bit is not kept across = or bare octal.

Mode of a file or directory created under a umask. A file starts from 666 and a directory from 777, then the umask bits are cleared. 022 makes a file 644 and a directory 755. masked lists the bits the umask turns off.

Whether one class may read, write, or execute under a mode. Pass the class that applies: on a real system the owner class is used for the owner even when the group bits differ. setuid, setgid and sticky do not grant the bit.
Bits that differ between two POSIX modes. added and removed run from the special bits down through owner, group and other. same is true when nothing differs.

Explain an IEEE 754 binary32 or binary64 value. Pass bits as hex, or a decimal or fraction, which is rounded ties-to-even. Returns the class, sign, unbiased exponent, fraction bits, and the exact value. Negative zero stays negative. The word nan is the quiet NaN; snan is the signaling NaN with payload 1. The top fraction bit is the quiet bit.

Round an exact decimal or fraction to binary32 or binary64. Modes are nearestEven, towardZero, towardPositive, and towardNegative. Ties in nearestEven go to an even fraction bit. Overflow becomes infinity, or the largest finite value when the mode points toward zero. underflow is set only when the result is subnormal or zero and not exact.

The next binary32 or binary64 value up or down. Positive zero and negative zero both step up to the smallest positive subnormal, and both step down to the smallest negative one. Infinity stays put at its end. A NaN is returned with its payload unchanged.

Unit in the last place of a binary32 or binary64 value. A power of two uses the spacing of its own binade. Zero uses the smallest subnormal. Infinity uses positive infinity. A NaN is returned with its payload unchanged.

IEEE 754 totalOrder on two binary32 or binary64 values. Negative zero is below positive zero. Negative NaNs are below minus infinity and positive NaNs are above plus infinity. A larger NaN payload is farther from zero. sameBits is true only when every bit matches. form bits reads both sides as hex; the default reads them as numbers rounded ties-to-even.

A written note or a MIDI number. Middle C is C4, which is 60. C-1 is 0 and G9 is 127. The name you pass keeps its spelling, so B#3 stays B#3 even though it is the same key as C4. sharp and flat are the two usual names of that key. x is a double sharp.

The interval between two written notes. The number comes from the letters and the quality from the semitones, so C to E is a major third and C to Fb is a diminished fourth. Direction follows the written notes. Semitones is negative when the second note is lower.

Move a written note by a named interval. The letter moves with the interval number, then the accidental is chosen to hit the semitones. A perfect third is rejected, and so is a quality that would need more than a double accidental. Up and down are the two directions.

Spell a scale on letters from a tonic. Major, minor, harmonic minor, melodic minor (the ascending form), the church modes, pentatonic, minor pentatonic, and blues. G# major is written with E# and F##, not with flats. signature lists the accidentals in scale order. The octave does not repeat the tonic.

exampleOutput.spelling: C4 D4 E4 F4 G4 A4 B4

endpoints.description: Spell a chord up from a root: major, minor, diminished, augmented, sus2, sus4, dom7, maj7, min7, dim7, half-dim7, and sixth. Letters stay in thirds except the suspensions and the sixth. A diminished seventh uses a double flat when the spelling needs it.

ISO 216 A, B and C sizes, plus the DL envelope, in millimeters. Portrait, so the width is the shorter side. Inches are exact millimeters divided by 25.4. A4 is 210 by 297. Set landscape to swap the sides.
The next larger and smaller sheet in the same ISO series. A4 sits between A3 and A5. A0 has no larger size and A10 has no smaller one. DL is not in a series.

How many copies of one sheet fit on another at full size. The copy may be turned. Two A4 pages fill an A3 and the waste is zero. count is 0 when it does not fit. orientation is how the copy sits, or none.
The largest scale that places one sheet on another, turning it when that lets it be larger. The scale is an exact ratio of the millimeter sides. Below one, the sheet has to shrink.

The smallest ISO C envelope that holds a sheet flat, and whether a DL envelope holds it flat or folded in exact thirds. C4 holds A4. DL does not hold A4 flat; it holds A4 folded in thirds. A sheet bigger than C0 has no C envelope.

Count the frames in an SMPTE timecode from midnight. Rates are 24, 25 and 30. A colon is non-drop and a semicolon is drop-frame, which is only legal at 30. Drop-frame skips 00 and 01 at the start of each minute except every tenth minute, so 01:00:00;00 is frame 107892 rather than 108000.
Write a frame count since midnight as SMPTE timecode. Set drop for 30 fps drop-frame. The count has to land inside one day. 30 frames at 30 fps is 00:00:01:00.
Add a signed frame count to a timecode and stay inside the same day. A result before midnight or at the next midnight is rejected. The semicolon, if present, keeps the result in drop-frame.
How many frames from one timecode to another, at the same rate. Positive means to is later. Both codes use a colon, or both use a semicolon. Mixing drop-frame with non-drop is rejected.

Exact length of a frame count. 24, 25 and non-drop 30 use 1/rate second per frame. Drop-frame 30 uses the NTSC frame, 1001/30000 second. Pass a timecode or a frame count, not both. The semicolon selects drop-frame when you pass a code.
CRC-16 over text or hex bytes. Algorithms are CCITT-FALSE, ARC, XMODEM, KERMIT and MODBUS. The check string 123456789 is 29b1 in CCITT-FALSE. This is not CRC-32.
Fletcher-16 checksum, modulus 255. The two sums are packed with the second sum in the high byte. "abcde" is c8f0.
Fletcher-32 checksum, modulus 65535. Bytes are big-endian 16-bit words. An odd final byte is padded with zero. "abcde" is 4ff029c7.
RFC 1071 internet checksum. Big-endian 16-bit words are added with end-around carry, then inverted. An odd final byte is padded with zero. The RFC example 0001 F203 F4F5 F6F7 is 220d.

The two historic Unix sums, matching GNU sum. bsd rotates the 16-bit sum right and counts 1024-byte blocks. sysv reduces modulo 65535, keeps 65535 when the total is a positive multiple of it, and counts 512-byte blocks. "123456789" is bsd 53615 and sysv 477.
Continued fraction of a non-negative rational, by the Euclidean algorithm. 13/8 is [1; 1, 1, 1, 2]. 355/113 is [3; 7, 16]. A trailing 1 is folded into the previous term, so this is the short form.
Exact value of a continued fraction [a0; a1, a2, ...]. Later terms are at least 1. [3; 7, 15, 1] and [3; 7, 16] are both 355/113. The canonical field is the short Euclidean form.
One convergent of a continued fraction. Index 0 is a0/1. The last index is the value itself. 13/8 at index 3 is 5/3.
Best rational approximation with a denominator up to maxDen. It searches the convergents and the intermediate fractions. 355/113 with maxDen 7 is 22/7. With maxDen 100 it is 311/99.

Continued fraction of a square root. sqrt(2) is [1; 2, 2, 2, ...] and the period is 1. sqrt(3) has period 2. A perfect square is one term and period 0. The period is the repeating length, even when fewer terms are requested.

Encode text as international Morse (ITU-R M.1677). Letters are separated by one space and words by " / ". SOS is ... --- ... Digits and the recommendation punctuation are included. Other characters are rejected.
Decode international Morse. Letters are separated by one space and words by " / ". The result is capitals. ... --- ... is SOS.
How long a Morse message takes at a given speed. The dit is 1200/wpm milliseconds. PARIS is 43 units, or 50 units once the trailing 7-unit word gap of a stream is added. SOS is 27 units.
Point on a cubic Bezier at t, as an exact fraction. t is between 0 and 1. The arch (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0) at one half is (1/2, 3/4).
Point on a quadratic Bezier at t, as an exact fraction. (0,0), (1,1), (2,0) at one half is (1, 1/2).
Split a quadratic or cubic Bezier at t by de Casteljau. Left and right are the two new control polygons, and they meet at the point on the curve.
Control points of the derivative of a quadratic or cubic Bezier. A cubic derivative is a quadratic, and each control is the degree times the step to the next point.
Tangent vector of a quadratic or cubic Bezier at t. It is the derivative curve evaluated at t. The arch (0,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0) at one half has tangent (3/2, 0).
Hamilton product of two quaternions, scalar first. i times j is k, and j times i is minus k. Components are exact fractions.
Conjugate and squared length of a quaternion. (1, 2, 3, 4) has squared length 30 and conjugate (1, -2, -3, -4). Unit means the squared length is 1.
Inverse of a quaternion, the conjugate divided by the squared length. (1, 2, 3, 4) inverts to (1/30, -1/15, -1/10, -2/15). Zero has no inverse.
Rotate a vector by a quaternion, q v q inverse. k sends (1, 0, 0) to (-1, 0, 0), a half turn about z. Scaling q does not change the turn.
Integer power of a quaternion. i squared is -1, and i to the fourth is 1. Exponent 0 is 1, including zero to the 0. A negative power inverts first.
Sign of a permutation of 0..n-1, from the number of inversions. [2, 1, 0] has three inversions and sign -1. The identity has sign 1.
Inverse of a permutation of 0..n-1. The inverse of [1, 2, 0] is [2, 0, 1]. Applying both is the identity.
Compose two permutations of the same length. a is applied first, then b, so the result at i is b[a[i]]. Both must use 0..n-1 once each.
The next permutation in lexicographic order. After [0, 1, 2] comes [0, 2, 1]. The reverse, [2, 1, 0], is the last and has no successor.
Lexicographic rank of a permutation, or the permutation at a rank. [0, 1, 2] is rank 0 and [2, 0, 1] is rank 4. Give the permutation, or n and a rank, not both. n is at most 10.

The nth Pell number. P0 is 0, P1 is 1, and each later term is twice the previous one plus the one before that. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 8192. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The nth companion Pell-Lucas number. Q0 and Q1 are both 2, and later terms use the Pell recurrence. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 8192. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth solution of the Pell equation x^2 - 2y^2 = (-1)^n. x is half the companion Pell-Lucas number and y is the Pell number. A supplied norm must equal that sign. n runs from 0 to 8192.
The sum of Pell numbers, or companion Pell-Lucas numbers, from lo through hi inclusive. seq is p or q. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 8192.
Compose two solutions of x^2 - 2y^2 = ±1. The unit for index a multiplied by the unit for index b is the unit for a+b. a+b must be at most 8192.
The binomial coefficient C(n, k). k must not exceed n, and both indexes run up to 4096. An optional modulus reduces the coefficient; zero is rejected. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth Catalan number. C0 and C1 are 1, C2 is 2, C3 is 5, and C_n = binom(2n, n) / (n+1). n runs from 0 to 2048. An optional modulus reduces the term; zero is rejected.
The ballot number B(n, k) = (n-k+1)/(n+1) * binom(n+k, k), for 0 <= k <= n. B(n, n) is the nth Catalan number. k above n is rejected. Both indexes run up to 2048.
Check a Dyck word of parentheses and report its semilength and height. The empty word is valid. A prefix that goes negative, or a word that does not close, is rejected.
The nth Motzkin number. M0 and M1 are 1, M2 is 2, M4 is 9, from M_n = sum binom(n, 2k) C_k. n runs from 0 to 512. An optional modulus reduces the term; zero is rejected.
base^exp mod m, exact, for a non-negative exponent. The modulus must be at least 1. A negative exponent is rejected. Decimals have no leading zeros and at most 200 digits.
The modular inverse of a modulo m, as a residue from 0 up to m-1. The modulus must be at least 1. A value that is not coprime to m is rejected.

Solve simultaneous congruences x ≡ a_i (mod m_i). Shared factors are allowed when the system is consistent; an inconsistent system is rejected. The result is the smallest non-negative solution and the lcm of the moduli.
The Jacobi symbol (a/n). n must be odd and positive. The value is -1, 0, or 1. An even or non-positive n is rejected.
Extended gcd of a and b. Returns g, x, and y with g = a*x + b*y and g >= 0. gcd(0, 0) is rejected. Decimals have no leading zeros.
The Pythagorean triple from m > n >= 1 and scale k >= 1. a is k(m^2-n^2), b is k(2mn), and c is k(m^2+n^2). primitive is true when k is 1, m and n are coprime, and they have opposite parity.
Check a^2 + b^2 = c^2 for positive integers, with c the hypotenuse. primitive is true when the three sides are coprime. A side triple that fails the equation is rejected.

Exact area data for a strict integer triangle. sixteen is 16 times the squared area. When sixteen is a perfect square, area is the reduced value of its square root over 4. A degenerate triple is rejected.
The cosine of the angle opposite side c, as a reduced rational (a^2+b^2-c^2)/(2ab). The sides must form a strict triangle. A right angle returns 0.
Classify a strict integer triangle. sides is equilateral, isosceles, or scalene. angles is acute, right, or obtuse, from comparing the squares of the sides. A degenerate triple is rejected.
Stern's diatomic sequence. s(0) is 0, s(1) is 1, even terms repeat s(n/2), and an odd term is the sum of its two neighbors in the previous row. An optional modulus reduces the term; zero is rejected.

The Calkin-Wilf tree. Give n to get the nth positive rational, starting at 1/1, or give a reduced num and den to get its index. The two answers must agree when both are sent. An unreduced fraction is rejected.
The mediant of a/b and c/d, which is (a+c)/(b+d) reduced by their gcd. Numerators may be zero. A non-positive denominator is rejected.
Whether a/b and c/d are Farey neighbors. They are adjacent when the determinant ad-bc is 1 or -1. A non-positive denominator is rejected.
The mediant child of a Farey-neighbor pair. a/b and c/d must satisfy |ad-bc| = 1. A pair that is not adjacent is rejected, as is a non-positive denominator.
The number of integer partitions p(n), from the pentagonal recurrence. p(0) is 1, p(5) is 7, and p(10) is 42. n runs from 0 to 2000. An optional modulus reduces the count; zero is rejected.

The number of partitions of n into distinct positive parts. This equals the number of partitions into odd parts. q(0) is 1 and q(5) is 3. n runs from 0 to 2000. An optional modulus reduces the count; zero is rejected.
The generalized pentagonal number n(3n-1)/2. n may be negative. n = 1 gives 1, n = -1 gives 2, and n = 0 is rejected. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The conjugate of an integer partition, read down the columns of its Ferrers diagram. Parts must be positive and nonincreasing. The empty partition is its own conjugate.
Check an integer partition and return its sum and length. Parts must be positive and nonincreasing. The empty list is the partition of zero. A rise or a zero part is rejected.

Convert an integer from one base to another. Bases run from 2 to 36, and letters may be any case. A digit that is not valid in the source base is rejected. The result is the digit string in the target base.
The sum of the decimal digits of an integer, ignoring the sign. 199 sums to 19. The decimal has no leading zeros. A malformed integer is rejected.
The digital root of a decimal integer. Zero stays zero, and any other magnitude is 1 + (n-1) mod 9, so multiples of 9 have root 9. The sign is ignored. A malformed integer is rejected.
Reverse the decimal digits of an integer. Leading zeros of the reversal are dropped, so 1200 becomes 21. The sign is kept. A malformed integer is rejected.
The repunit of length n, (10^n - 1)/9. R1 is 1 and R2 is 11. n = 0 is rejected. n runs up to 500. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Encode a non-negative integer as a binary reflected Gray code. The code is n xor (n shifted right by one). Zero stays zero, and a negative integer is rejected.
Decode a binary reflected Gray code back to its index. The walk xors the code with each of its right shifts. A negative code is rejected.
The next binary reflected Gray code after g. It is the code of the index one past the index of g. A negative code is rejected.
The single bit that flips in the binary reflected Gray code when the index goes from n to n+1. Bit 0 is the least significant bit. A negative index is rejected.
The binary reflected Gray code of n, written in exactly width bits. Bit 0 is on the right. n must be smaller than 2^width. A width that cannot hold n is rejected.
Add two integer polynomials, lowest degree first. Trailing zeros are dropped, and the zero polynomial is an empty list. An optional modulus reduces each coefficient; zero is rejected.

Multiply two integer polynomials, lowest degree first. The zero polynomial is an empty list. An optional modulus reduces each coefficient; zero is rejected. A coefficient past 15 digits is a decimal string.
Evaluate an integer polynomial at an integer point, by Horner. The zero polynomial evaluates to 0. An optional modulus reduces the result; zero is rejected.
Differentiate an integer polynomial. The derivative of a constant is the zero polynomial, which is an empty list. An optional modulus reduces each coefficient; zero is rejected.
Exact quotient of two integer polynomials. The divisor must be non-zero, and every leading step must divide in the integers. A zero divisor or a non-integral quotient is rejected.
Euler totient phi(n), the count of integers from 1 to n that are coprime to n. phi(1) is 1. n = 0 is rejected. n runs up to 10^12.
The Mobius function mu(n). It is 0 when n has a squared prime factor, and otherwise (-1)^k for k distinct primes. mu(1) is 1. n = 0 is rejected.
The number of positive divisors of n. A prime has 2, and d(1) is 1. n = 0 is rejected. n runs up to 10^12.
The sum of the positive divisors of n. sigma(6) is 12 and sigma(28) is 56. n = 0 is rejected. A value past 15 digits is a decimal string.
Whether n is prime, by trial division. 1 is not prime. n < 1 is rejected. n runs up to 10^12.
The greedy Egyptian fraction for a proper positive fraction a/b. 5/6 is 1/2 + 1/3. A fraction that is not strictly between 0 and 1 is rejected.
The reduced sum of unit fractions 1/d. Dens must be positive. An empty list or a non-positive denominator is rejected.
The nth harmonic number as a reduced fraction. H1 is 1/1, H2 is 3/2, and H6 is 49/20. n < 1 is rejected. n runs up to 200.
The nth Sylvester number. s(0) is 2, and each later term is s*(s-1)+1. A negative index is rejected. n runs up to 8. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Check that a sum of unit fractions equals the fraction a/b. A match returns the reduced sum. A sum that differs, or a non-positive denominator, is rejected.

The nth Jacobsthal number. J0 is 0, J1 is 1, and each later term is the previous one plus twice the one before that. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 8192. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The nth Jacobsthal-Lucas number. L0 is 2, L1 is 1, and later terms use the Jacobsthal recurrence. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 8192. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Jacobsthal numbers, or Jacobsthal-Lucas numbers, from lo through hi inclusive. seq is j or l. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 8192.
The Jacobsthal addition rule. (L(a)*J(b) + J(a)*L(b)) / 2 is J(a+b). a+b must be at most 8192.
The power identity J(n) + J(n+1) = 2^n. left is J(n), right is J(n+1), and value is their sum. n runs from 0 to 8191 so that n+1 stays in range. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The nth Padovan number. P0, P1, and P2 are 1, and each later term is the sum of the term two back and the term three back. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 8192. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The nth Perrin number. R0 is 3, R1 is 0, R2 is 2, and later terms use the Padovan recurrence. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 8192. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Padovan numbers, or Perrin numbers, from lo through hi inclusive. seq is p or r. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 8192.
The remainder of the nth Perrin number divided by n. A prime n divides R(n), so the remainder is 0. n runs from 1 to 8192. Past 15 digits the Perrin number is a decimal string.
The Padovan step identity P(n) = P(n-1) + P(n-5). left is P(n-1) and right is P(n-5). n runs from 5 to 8192. Past 15 digits a term is a decimal string.

The Stirling number of the second kind S(n,k), the number of ways to partition n objects into k nonempty unlabeled sets. S(5,2) is 15. S(n,k) is 0 when k is greater than n. n and k run from 0 to 80. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth Bell number, the number of partitions of a set of n objects. B(0) and B(1) are 1, and B(5) is 52. n runs from 0 to 80. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Row n of Stirling numbers of the second kind, from S(n,0) through S(n,n), plus the Bell number that sums the row. n runs from 0 to 80. Past 15 digits an entry is a decimal string.
The sum of Bell numbers from lo through hi inclusive. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 80. Past 15 digits the sum is a decimal string.
The Stirling recurrence S(n,k) = k*S(n-1,k) + S(n-1,k-1). term is the first summand and diag is the second. n and k run from 1 to 80. Past 15 digits a part is a decimal string.
The Delannoy number D(m,n), the number of paths from (0,0) to (m,n) using steps (1,0), (0,1), and (1,1). D(3,5) is 231. m and n run from 0 to 64. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The central Delannoy number D(n,n). D(0,0) is 1 and D(3,3) is 63. n runs from 0 to 64. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth large Schröder number. S(0) is 1, S(1) is 2, and S(5) is 394. n runs from 0 to 64. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth little Schröder number. It is 1 at n = 0 and half the large Schröder number for n > 0. s(5) is 197. n runs from 0 to 64. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Delannoy numbers D(m,0) through D(m,hi). The sum through D(4,4) is 501. m and hi run from 0 to 64. Past 15 digits the sum is a decimal string.
The Narayana number N(n,k). N(5,3) is 20. A k outside 1..n yields 0. n runs from 1 to 60 and k from 0 to 60. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Narayana numbers N(n,1) through N(n,n). Their sum is the Catalan number C(n). The row for n = 4 is 1, 6, 6, 1 and sums to 14. n runs from 1 to 60.
The Narayana product C(n,k)*C(n,k-1). It is exactly n times N(n,k). product is that binomial product and value is the Narayana number. n runs from 1 to 60.
The Fuss-Catalan number C(p*n+1, n) / (p*n+1). FC(2,n) is the Catalan number, so FC(2,5) is 42. p runs from 1 to 8 and n from 0 to 30. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The Fuss-Catalan division. num is C(p*n+1, n), den is p*n+1, and value is the exact quotient. p runs from 1 to 8 and n from 0 to 30. Past 15 digits a part is a decimal string.

The Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind T(n,x) at an integer x. T(0,x) is 1, T(1,x) is x, and T(2,3) is 17. n runs from 0 to 64 and x from -1000 to 1000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The Chebyshev polynomial of the second kind U(n,x) at an integer x. U(0,x) is 1, U(1,x) is 2*x, and U(3,2) is 56. n runs from 0 to 64 and x from -1000 to 1000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The Chebyshev discriminant identity T(n,x)^2 - (x^2-1)*U(n-1,x)^2 = 1. gap is that difference. n runs from 1 to 64. Past 15 digits t or u is a decimal string.
The product identity 2*T(a,x)*T(b,x) = T(a+b,x) + T(|a-b|,x). twice is the left side and sum is the right side. a+b must be at most 64.
One step of the Chebyshev recurrence. kind is t or u. prev is degree n-1, older is degree n-2, and value is 2*x*prev - older. n runs from 2 to 64.

The nth Tribonacci number. T0 and T1 are 0, T2 is 1, and each later term is the sum of the previous three. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Tribonacci numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from T0 through T10 is 177. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 4096.
The Tribonacci step T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) + T(n-3). left is T(n-3), mid is T(n-2), and right is T(n-1). n runs from 3 to 4096. Past 15 digits a term is a decimal string.

The smallest index n with T(n) equal to value. 0 is index 0, and 1 is index 2. A number that is not a Tribonacci term, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 600 digits.
T(n) mod m. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. The residue is smaller than the modulus.
The nth Thue-Morse bit, the parity of the number of 1-bits in n. t(0) is 0, t(1) is 1, and t(2) is 1. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The number of 1-bits in the Thue-Morse sequence from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from t(0) through t(7) is 4. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 1000000.
The first n Thue-Morse bits as a string of 0 and 1. The first 8 bits are 01101001. n runs from 1 to 4096.

Find a cube in a 0/1 string, a block xxx. 000 is a cube at index 0 of length 1. A Thue-Morse prefix has no cube. An empty string or a character other than 0 or 1 is rejected. The string stops at 512 characters.
The number of 1s in t(0) through t(n), and the bit t(n) itself. Through n = 7 the weight is 4. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The Rudin-Shapiro bit of n, the parity of the number of overlapping 11 blocks in its binary expansion. n = 3 is 11, so the bit is 1 and the sign is -1. n = 0 is 0. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The Baum-Sweet bit of n. It is 1 when every run of 0s in the binary expansion has even length, and 0 when some run of 0s has odd length. b(0) is 1 and b(2) is 0. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The regular paperfolding bit of n. Write n = m * 2^k with m odd. The bit is 1 when m is 1 mod 4, and 0 when m is 3 mod 4. The first three bits, from n = 1, are 1, 1, 0. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The Golay-Rudin-Shapiro partial sum. Each term is +1 or -1 as the Rudin-Shapiro sign of k, and the value is the sum from k = 0 through n. The sum through n = 3 is 2. n runs from 0 to 100000.
The Thue-Morse run that contains n. The bit is the parity of the 1-bits of n. A run has length 1 or 2. Index 0 is a run of one 0, and index 1 starts a run of two 1s. n runs from 0 to 1000000.

The nth Lucas number. L0 is 2, L1 is 1, and each later term is the sum of the previous two. L5 is 11 and L10 is 123. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Lucas numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from L0 through L5 is 28. The sum equals L(hi+2) - L(lo+1). lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 4096.
The smallest index n with L(n) equal to value. 2 is index 0, and 1 is index 1. A number that is not a Lucas number, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 600 digits.
L(n) mod m. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. The residue is smaller than the modulus.
The Lucas discriminant L(n)^2 - 5*F(n)^2, which equals 4*(-1)^n. F is the Fibonacci sequence with F0 = 0 and F1 = 1. For n = 5 the value is -4. n runs from 0 to 4096.
The ruler value of n, the exponent of 2 in n. v2(1) is 0, v2(8) is 3, and v2(12) is 2. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The sum of the ruler values v2(1) through v2(n). It equals n minus the number of 1-bits in n. The sum through 15 is 11. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The ruler values v2(1) through v2(n), written as comma-separated integers. The first 8 values are 0,1,0,2,0,1,0,3. n runs from 1 to 4096.

The largest ruler value on 1 through n, and the smallest index where it occurs. That index is the greatest power of 2 that does not exceed n. On 1 through 20 the maximum is 4, at 16. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Remove every factor of 2 from n. The odd part of 12 is 3 and the valuation is 2. The odd part of 7 is 7. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
One Collatz step. An even n is halved and an odd n becomes 3n+1. 6 goes to 3, and 1 goes to 4. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The number of Collatz steps from n until 1. The length of 1 is 0, the length of 6 is 8, and the length of 27 is 111. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The largest value on the Collatz trajectory from n through 1, including n. The peak of 1 is 1, the peak of 6 is 16, and the peak of 27 is 9232. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The parity of each term on the Collatz trajectory from n through 1. 0 is even and 1 is odd. The parity of 6 is 010100001. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The Collatz glide of n, the number of steps until a value strictly below n. The glide of 1 is 0, the glide of 6 is 1, and the glide of 7 is 11. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The nth lower Wythoff number, floor(n*phi), where phi is (1+sqrt(5))/2. A(1) is 1, A(2) is 3, and A(5) is 8. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The nth upper Wythoff number, floor(n*phi^2), which is A(n)+n. B(1) is 2, B(2) is 5, and B(5) is 13. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The nth Wythoff pair. lower is floor(n*phi) and upper is lower+n. The pair for n = 1 is 1 and 2. The pair for n = 5 is 8 and 13. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Which Wythoff sequence contains m, and at which index. 1 is the lower number at index 1. 2 is the upper number at index 1. Every positive integer is in exactly one sequence. m runs from 1 to 1600000.
