The Beatty term floor(n*sqrt(d)). floor(5*sqrt(2)) is 7, and floor(2*sqrt(3)) is 3. n runs from 0 to 1000000 and d runs from 1 to 1000000.
The nth Kolakoski term, using a 1-based index. The sequence is 1s and 2s, and it starts 1, 2, 2, 1, 1. Term 7 is 1. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The first n Kolakoski terms as a string of the digits 1 and 2. The first 10 terms are 1221121221. n runs from 1 to 4096.
The sum of the first n Kolakoski terms. The sum of the first 10 terms is 15. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The Kolakoski run that contains the 1-based index n. A run has length 1 or 2. Index 1 is a single 1. Index 2 starts two 2s. n runs from 1 to 100000.
Whether a string of the digits 1 and 2 is a prefix of the Kolakoski sequence. 122112 is a prefix. An empty string, or any other character, is rejected. The string stops at 512 characters.
Carmichael's lambda of n, the exponent of the multiplicative group mod n. lambda(1) is 1, lambda(8) is 2, lambda(p) is p-1, and lambda(15) is 4. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The Jordan totient J(k, n). J(1, n) is Euler's totient. J(1, 6) is 2 and J(2, 6) is 24. k runs from 1 to 12 and n runs from 1 to 1000000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Dedekind's psi function, n times the product of (1+1/p) over the distinct prime factors of n. psi(1) is 1, psi(2) is 3, and psi(6) is 12. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The aliquot part of n, the sum of proper divisors. The aliquot part of 1 is 0, of 9 is 4, and of 6 is 6. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Classify n from its divisor sum. 6 and 28 are perfect. 12 is abundant. 8 is deficient. The class is perfect, abundant, or deficient. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.

The physicist Hermite polynomial H(n, x) at an integer x. H(0, x) is 1, H(1, x) is 2x, H(2, 1) is 2, and H(3, 1) is -4. n runs from 0 to 32 and x from -1000 to 1000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The probabilist Hermite polynomial He(n, x) at an integer x. He(0, x) is 1, He(1, x) is x, and He(2, 1) is 0. n runs from 0 to 32 and x from -1000 to 1000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The Laguerre polynomial L(n, x) at an integer x, as a reduced fraction. L(n, 0) is 1, L(1, 1) is 0, and L(2, 1) is -1/2. n runs from 0 to 32 and x from -1000 to 1000.
The Legendre polynomial P(n, x) at an integer x, as a reduced fraction. P(n, 1) is 1, and P(2, 2) is 11/2. n runs from 0 to 32 and x from -1000 to 1000.
The derivative of the physicist Hermite polynomial, H'(n, x) = 2*n*H(n-1, x). At n = 3 and x = 1 the derivative is 12. n runs from 1 to 32 and x from -1000 to 1000.

The signed Stirling number of the first kind s(n, k). s(4, 2) is 11 and s(5, 2) is -50. s(n, 0) is 0 for n > 0. n runs from 0 to 64, and k must not pass n. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The unsigned Stirling number of the first kind, the absolute value of s(n, k). It counts permutations of n with k cycles. c(5, 2) is 50 and c(5, 1) is 24. n runs from 0 to 64.
Row n of the signed Stirling numbers of the first kind, from s(n, 0) through s(n, n). The absolute values sum to n!. Row 4 is 0, -6, 11, -6, 1. n runs from 0 to 64.
One step of s(n, k) = s(n-1, k-1) - (n-1)*s(n-1, k). For n = 5 and k = 2, the previous term is -6, the scaled term is 44, and the value is -50. n runs from 1 to 64 and k from 1 to n.
The subfactorial !n, the number of derangements of n objects. !0 is 1, !1 is 0, !2 is 1, and !5 is 44. n runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The Zeckendorf representation of n. Fibonacci numbers start F1 = 1, F2 = 1, F3 = 2, and no two used indices are consecutive. 4 is F4 + F2, and 100 is F11 + F6 + F4. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.

Sum Fibonacci numbers by index, using F1 = 1 and F2 = 1. Indices must be at least 2 and no two may be consecutive. Indices 11, 6, and 4 sum to 100. An empty list is rejected. At most 64 indices, each at most 512.
The Zeckendorf bit string of n, from the largest used Fibonacci index down to F2. The bit string of 1 is 1, of 4 is 101, and of 100 is 1000010100. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The nth bit of the infinite Fibonacci word, starting at n = 0. The word is the fixed point of 0 to 01 and 1 to 0, and it starts 01001010. n runs from 0 to 99999.
The first n bits of the Fibonacci word. The first 8 bits are 01001010, and the first 16 bits are 0100101001001010. n runs from 1 to 4096.
The number of distinct prime factors of n. omega(1) is 0, omega(4) is 1, and omega(30) is 3. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The number of prime factors of n counted with multiplicity. Omega(1) is 0, Omega(4) is 2, and Omega(12) is 3. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The radical of n, the product of its distinct prime factors. rad(1) is 1, rad(12) is 6, and rad(36) is 6. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The sum of prime factors of n with multiplicity. sopfr(1) is 0, sopfr(12) is 7, and sopfr(36) is 10. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n is squarefree, together with its radical. 1 and 30 are squarefree. 4 and 12 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The nth Bernoulli number as a reduced fraction, from the Akiyama-Tanigawa algorithm. B0 is 1, B1 is 1/2, B2 is 1/6, and B4 is -1/30. Odd indices after 1 are 0. n runs from 0 to 40.
The von Staudt denominator of B(m) for even m at least 2: the product of primes p such that p-1 divides m. The denominator of B2 is 6, and of B4 is 30. An odd m is rejected. m runs from 2 to 40.
The von Staudt-Clausen integer. For even m at least 2, B(m) plus the sum of 1/p over primes p with p-1 dividing m is an integer. For m = 2, 4, 6, and 10 that integer is 1. An odd m is rejected.
The nth tangent number. T1 is 1, T2 is 2, T3 is 16, and T4 is 272. It is read from the Bernoulli number B(2n). n runs from 1 to 20. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Bernoulli numbers B0 through Bn, as a reduced fraction. The sum through B1 is 3/2, and through B2 is 5/3. n runs from 0 to 40.
The integer square root of a non-negative decimal integer, the greatest r with r^2 not exceeding n. isqrt(0) is 0 and isqrt(10) is 3. A leading zero is rejected. n has at most 600 digits.
The integer cube root of a non-negative decimal integer, the greatest r with r^3 not exceeding n. icbrt(26) is 2 and icbrt(27) is 3. A leading zero is rejected. n has at most 600 digits.
Whether a non-negative decimal integer is a perfect square, and the root when it is. 16 is 4 squared. 15 is not a square. A leading zero is rejected. n has at most 600 digits.
The integer power base^exp. 2^10 is 1024, and (-2)^5 is -32. 0^0 is 1. exp runs from 0 to 256. The base has at most 80 digits. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

Whether n is a perfect power a^k with k at least 2. The base is the smallest such a, so the exponent is the largest. 16 is 2^4, 36 is 6^2, and 7 is not a perfect power. 0 and 1 use exponent 2. A leading zero is rejected. n has at most 80 digits.
The nth Recamán term. a(0) is 0. Each later term steps back by n when that value is positive and new, and otherwise steps forward by n. a(4) is 2 and a(6) is 13. n runs from 0 to 100000.
Whether value appears in Recamán's sequence from a(0) through a(limit), and the smallest index if it does. 2 appears at index 4. 4 does not appear by index 20. limit runs from 0 to 100000.
The nth Golomb term, 1-based. a(1) is 1, a(n) counts how often n will appear, and a(6) is 4. The sequence starts 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The sum of the first n Golomb terms, from a(1) through a(n). The sum of the first 5 terms is 11. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The smallest index n with Golomb a(n) equal to k. Index 1 holds 1, index 4 holds 3, and index 6 holds 4. k runs from 1 to 5000.
The hockey-stick sum of binomial coefficients C(i, r) from i = r through n. It equals C(n+1, r+1). The sum for r = 2 and n = 5 is 20. r must not pass n. Both run from 0 to 1024.
The Vandermonde convolution. The sum of C(m, k)*C(n, r-k) equals C(m+n, r). For m = 3, n = 3, and r = 2 the value is 15. m and n run from 0 to 256, and r must not pass m+n.
The number of ways to place n identical items into k distinct bins, which is C(n+k-1, n). Three items in two bins can be placed in 4 ways. n runs from 0 to 1024 and k runs from 1 to 1024.

The number of ways to choose k elements from n types with repetition, which is C(n+k-1, k). Choosing 2 from 3 types can be done in 6 ways. Choosing nothing can be done in 1 way. n and k run from 0 to 1024.

The number of carries when a and b are added in prime base p. By Kummer, that is the exponent of p in C(a+b, a). Adding 5 and 3 in base 2 makes 3 carries. A composite base is rejected. a and b run from 0 to 1000000000000, and p runs from 2 to 1000000.

The double factorial n!!. Even n uses the even factors down to 2, and odd n uses the odd factors down to 1. 0!! is 1, 6!! is 48, and 7!! is 105. n runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The primorial of n, the product of the primes less than or equal to n. The primorial of 1 is 1, of 10 is 210, and of 11 is 2310. n runs from 1 to 5000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The falling factorial (n)_k = n*(n-1)*...*(n-k+1). (5)_3 is 60, (5)_0 is 1, and (5)_6 is 0. n runs from 0 to 100000 and k runs from 0 to 512. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The rising factorial n^(k) = n*(n+1)*...*(n+k-1). 5^(3) is 210, and 5^(0) is 1. n runs from 0 to 100000 and k runs from 0 to 512. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
n! mod m. 0! is 1, so 0! mod 5 is 1. 10! mod 97 is 30. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 100000.
The product of two integer 2 by 2 matrices, each written as [a, b, c, d]. [1, 1, 0, 1] times [1, 0, 1, 1] is [2, 1, 1, 1]. Each entry runs from -1000000 to 1000000.

The non-negative integer power of a 2 by 2 integer matrix. The exponent 0 is the identity [1, 0, 0, 1]. [1, 1, 0, 1] to the fifth is [1, 5, 0, 1]. [1, 1, 1, 0] to the fifth is [8, 5, 5, 3]. The exponent runs from 0 to 64.
The determinant ad-bc of a 2 by 2 integer matrix [a, b, c, d]. The determinant of [1, 1, 0, 1] is 1, and the determinant of [2, 0, 0, 3] is 6.
The inverse of a 2 by 2 integer matrix whose determinant is 1 or -1. The inverse of [1, 1, 0, 1] is [1, -1, 0, 1]. Any other determinant is rejected.
The trace a+d of a 2 by 2 integer matrix [a, b, c, d]. The trace of [1, 1, 0, 1] is 2, and the trace of [8, 5, 5, 3] is 11.

The Frobenius number of two coprime integers a and b, each at least 2. It is ab-a-b, the largest integer that cannot be made with non-negative combinations. For 2 and 5 it is 3. For 4 and 7 it is 17. A pair that is not coprime is rejected.
How many positive integers cannot be made with coprime denominations a and b. The count is (a-1)*(b-1)/2. For 2 and 5 it is 2. For 4 and 7 it is 9. A pair that is not coprime is rejected.
Whether n can be made with non-negative counts of coins a and b. 10 can be made with 2 and 5. 3 cannot. 0 can. a and b run from 1 to 10000, and n runs from 0 to 100000.

The number of non-negative integer solutions of a*x + b*y = n. Order of summands does not matter. There are 2 ways to make 10 with 2 and 5, and 0 ways to make 3. a and b run from 1 to 10000, and n runs from 0 to 100000.
The fewest coins of denominations a and b that sum to n. Making 10 with 2 and 5 takes 2 coins. An amount that cannot be made is rejected. a and b run from 1 to 10000, and n runs from 0 to 100000.
The nth look-and-say term, starting from 1. Term 1 is 1, term 4 is 1211, and term 5 is 111221. Each run of k copies of a digit d becomes the digits of k followed by d. n runs from 1 to 25.

One look-and-say step on a digit string. 1 becomes 11, and 1211 becomes 111221. Two 2s become 22. An empty string, or a character that is not a digit, is rejected. The string stops at 4096 characters.
The number of digits in the nth look-and-say term, starting from 1. Term 1 has length 1, term 5 has length 6, and term 8 has length 10. n runs from 1 to 25.
One digit of the nth look-and-say term. The index starts at 0. Term 5 is 111221, so index 3 is 2. An index past the end is rejected. n runs from 1 to 25.

How many times a digit occurs in the nth look-and-say term. Term 5 is 111221, so it has four 1s and two 2s. A digit from 4 through 9 occurs zero times in the classic sequence. n runs from 1 to 25, and the digit runs from 0 to 9.
The nth Hofstadter Q term. Q(1) and Q(2) are 1, and Q(n) = Q(n-Q(n-1)) + Q(n-Q(n-2)). Q(10) is 6, and Q(16) is 9. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The sum of Hofstadter Q terms Q(1) through Q(n). The sum through Q(10) is 36, and the sum through Q(20) is 129. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The first n Hofstadter Q terms, from Q(1) through Q(n), written as comma-separated integers. The first 10 terms are 1,1,2,3,3,4,5,5,6,6. n runs from 1 to 4096.
The nth Hofstadter G term. G(0) is 0, and G(n) = n - G(G(n-1)). G(1) is 1, and G(10) is 6. n runs from 0 to 100000.
The nth Hofstadter H term. H(0) is 0, and H(n) = n - H(H(H(n-1))). H(1) is 1, and H(10) is 7. n runs from 0 to 100000.
The nth Hofstadter-Conway term. a(1) and a(2) are 1, and a(n) = a(a(n-1)) + a(n-a(n-1)). a(5) is 3, and a(10) is 6. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The sum of Hofstadter-Conway terms a(1) through a(n). The sum through a(10) is 32, and the sum through a(30) is 266. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The nth Hofstadter male term. M(0) is 0, F(0) is 1, M(n) = n - F(M(n-1)), and F(n) = n - M(F(n-1)). M(2) is 1, and M(5) is 3. n runs from 0 to 100000.
The nth Hofstadter female term. F(0) is 1, M(0) is 0, F(n) = n - M(F(n-1)), and M(n) = n - F(M(n-1)). F(1) is 1, and F(5) is 3. n runs from 0 to 100000.
The Hofstadter male and female terms at the same index. M(0) is 0 and F(0) is 1. At n = 5 both terms are 3. n runs from 0 to 100000.

The nth Tetranacci number. T0, T1, and T2 are 0, T3 is 1, and each later term is the sum of the previous four. T(10) is 56. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Tetranacci numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from T0 through T10 is 116. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
T(n) mod m for the Tetranacci sequence. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. The residue is smaller than the modulus.

The smallest index n with T(n) equal to value. 0 is index 0, and 1 is index 3. A number that is not a Tetranacci term, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 600 digits.
The Tetranacci step T(n) = T(n-1) + T(n-2) + T(n-3) + T(n-4). a is T(n-4), b is T(n-3), c is T(n-2), and d is T(n-1). n runs from 4 to 4096. Past 15 digits a term is a decimal string.

The nth Pentanacci number. P0 through P3 are 0, P4 is 1, and each later term is the sum of the previous five. P(10) is 31. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Pentanacci numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from P0 through P12 is 244. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
P(n) mod m for the Pentanacci sequence. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. The residue is smaller than the modulus.

The smallest index n with P(n) equal to value. 0 is index 0, and 1 is index 4. A number that is not a Pentanacci term, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 600 digits.

The Pentanacci step P(n) = P(n-1) + P(n-2) + P(n-3) + P(n-4) + P(n-5). a is P(n-5), b is P(n-4), c is P(n-3), d is P(n-2), and e is P(n-1). n runs from 5 to 4096. Past 15 digits a term is a decimal string.

The nth Leonardo number. L(0) and L(1) are 1, and L(n) = L(n-1) + L(n-2) + 1. L(4) is 9, and L(10) is 177. An optional modulus reduces the term, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Leonardo numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from L(0) through L(5) is 34. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
L(n) mod m for the Leonardo sequence. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 4096. The residue is smaller than the modulus.

The smallest index n with L(n) equal to value. 1 is index 0, and 9 is index 4. A number that is not a Leonardo number, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 600 digits.

The Leonardo identity L(n) = 2*F(n+1) - 1. F is the Fibonacci sequence with F(0) = 0 and F(1) = 1. For n = 10, L is 177 and F(11) is 89, so the difference is 0. n runs from 0 to 4096. Past 15 digits a term is a decimal string.

The nth Euler zigzag number, the number of up-down permutations of n. a(0) is 1, a(3) is 2, a(4) is 5, and a(5) is 16. For n at least 1 it is the Entringer number E(n, n). n runs from 0 to 40. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Euler zigzag numbers a(0) through a(n). The sum through a(5) is 26, and the sum through a(10) is 60201. n runs from 0 to 40. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The Entringer number E(n, k). E(1, 1) is 1, and E(n, k) = E(n, k-1) + E(n-1, n-k). E(5, 2) is 10, and E(6, 3) is 46. The last entry E(n, n) is the zigzag number a(n). n and k run from 1 to 40, and k must not pass n.

The nth Genocchi number |G(2n)|, from G(2n) = 2*(1-4^n)*B(2n) with B(1) = +1/2. The first four absolute values are 1, 1, 3, and 17. signed is (-1)^n times that value. n runs from 1 to 20. Past 15 digits a value is a decimal string.
The nth secant number, the signed Euler number E(2n) = (-1)^n * a(2n). E(0) is 1, E(2) is -1, E(4) is 5, and E(6) is -61. n runs from 0 to 20. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The number of involutions of n objects. I(0) and I(1) are 1, and I(n) = I(n-1) + (n-1)*I(n-2). I(5) is 26, and I(10) is 9496. n runs from 0 to 100. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of involution numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from I(0) through I(10) is 13232. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 100. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
I(n) mod m, the involution number reduced by a positive modulus. Zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 100. The residue is smaller than the modulus.
The rencontres number D(n, k), the permutations of n objects with k fixed points. D(n, k) = C(n, k) * !(n-k). D(5, 0) is 44, and D(5, 2) is 20. n runs from 0 to 100, and k runs from 0 to n.

The number of involutions of n objects with exactly k fixed points. It is 0 when n-k is odd. For n = 5 and k = 1 the count is 15, and for n = 5 and k = 5 it is 1. n runs from 0 to 100, and k runs from 0 to n. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth Fubini number, the ordered partitions of an n-element set. a(0) is 1, a(2) is 3, a(3) is 13, and a(5) is 541. n runs from 0 to 20. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Fubini numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from a(0) through a(5) is 634. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 20. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth Fubini number mod m. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 20. The residue is smaller than the modulus.

The unsigned Lah number L(n, k). L(0, 0) is 1, L(n, 0) is 0 for n > 0, and L(n, 1) is n!. L(5, 2) is 240, and L(6, 3) is 1200. n and k run from 0 to 20, and k must not pass n. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

Row n of the unsigned Lah numbers, from L(n, 0) through L(n, n), written as comma-separated integers. Row 5 is 0,120,240,120,20,1. n runs from 0 to 12. Past 15 digits a term inside the row is still written in decimal.

The nth Riordan number. R(0) is 1, R(1) is 0, and (n+1)*R(n) = (n-1)*(2*R(n-1) + 3*R(n-2)) for n at least 2. R(4) is 3, and R(6) is 15. n runs from 0 to 80. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Riordan numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from R(0) through R(10) is 989. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 80. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
R(n) mod m for the Riordan numbers. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 80. The residue is smaller than the modulus.

The nth Fine number. F(0) is 1, F(1) is 0, F(2) is 1, and F(6) is 57. For n at least 1, F(n) = C(n) - sum of C(i)*F(n-1-i) over i from 0 to n-1, with C the Catalan numbers. n runs from 0 to 80. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of Fine numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from F(0) through F(6) is 85. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 80. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The period-doubling bit at index n, starting at 0. It is the parity of the exponent of 2 in n+1. Bit 0 is 0, bit 1 is 1, and the first 8 bits are 01000101. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
The first n period-doubling bits, as a string of the digits 0 and 1. The first 8 bits are 01000101. n runs from 1 to 4096.
The number of 1s in the first n period-doubling bits, from index 0 through n-1. The first 8 bits have three 1s, and the first 100 bits have 33. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
The Cantor bit of n. It is 1 when every base-3 digit of n is 0 or 1, and 0 when a digit is 2. Bit 0 is 1, bit 2 is 0, and bit 4 is 1. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
How many integers from 0 through n have only the digits 0 and 1 in base 3. The count through 0 is 1, through 2 is 2, and through 8 is 4. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
How many integer pairs (x, y), counting order and signs, satisfy x^2 + y^2 = n. There is 1 for 0, 4 for 1, and 8 for 5. n runs from 0 to 1000000000000.

Nonnegative integers x and y with x <= y and x^2 + y^2 = n, choosing the greatest y. 5 is 1 and 2. 25 is 0 and 5. A number that is not a sum of two squares is rejected. n runs from 0 to 1000000000000.

Whether n is a sum of three integer squares, and one nonnegative witness x <= y <= z when it is. It is impossible exactly when n = 4^power * odd with odd congruent to 7 mod 8. 3 is 1, 1, 1. 7 is impossible. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
Four nonnegative integers w <= x <= y <= z with w^2 + x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = n. Every nonnegative integer has one. 7 is 1, 1, 1, 2. n runs from 0 to 1000000.

Write n = 4^power * odd, with odd not divisible by 4. blocked is true when odd is congruent to 7 mod 8, which is exactly when n is not a sum of three squares. 7 and 28 are blocked. 6 is not. n runs from 0 to 1000000000000.
Liouville's function lambda(n) = (-1) to the number of prime factors of n, counted with multiplicity. lambda(1) is 1, lambda(2) is -1, and lambda(4) is 1. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The sum of Liouville's lambda(k) from 1 through n. The sum through 10 is 0, and the sum through 30 is -4. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The Mertens function M(n), the sum of the Mobius function mu(k) from 1 through n. M(1) is 1, M(10) is -1, and M(100) is 1. n runs from 1 to 1000000.

The largest absolute value of the Mertens function M(k) for k from 1 through n, and the smallest k where it occurs. Through 10 the maximum is 2 at k = 5. Through 100 it is 4 at k = 31. n runs from 1 to 1000000.

If n is a prime power p^k with k at least 1, return that prime and the exponent. Otherwise the prime and the exponent are 0. 8 is 2^3, 49 is 7^2, and 12 is not a prime power. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The largest square dividing n. 1 gives 1, 8 gives 4, 12 gives 4, and 18 gives 9. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
n divided by its largest square factor. 12 gives 3, 18 gives 2, 36 gives 1, and 45 gives 5. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n is powerful: 1, or every prime factor's exponent is at least 2. 1, 8, and 36 are powerful. 12 is not. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n is cubefull: 1, or every prime factor's exponent is at least 3. 1 and 8 are cubefull. 36 is powerful but not cubefull. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n is an Achilles number: powerful, but not a perfect power. 72 and 108 are Achilles. 36 is a square, and 1 is a perfect power, so neither is Achilles. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.

The sum of the kth powers of the divisors of n. sigma_2(1) is 1, sigma_2(6) is 50, and sigma_2(12) is 210. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000, and k runs from 2 to 12. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The abundancy sigma(n)/n as a reduced fraction. 1 is 1/1, 4 is 7/4, 6 is 2/1, and 12 is 7/3. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The deficiency 2n - sigma(n). A deficient number is positive, a perfect number is 0, and an abundant number is negative. 4 is 1, 6 is 0, and 12 is -4. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The sum of the unitary divisors of n. A unitary divisor shares no prime factor with the complementary divisor. The sum is 1 for 1, 12 for 6, 20 for 12, and 72 for 30. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
How many unitary divisors n has. The count is 2 to the number of distinct prime factors, and 1 has one unitary divisor. 7 has 2, 12 has 4, and 30 has 8. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Follow the happy-number map: replace n by the sum of the squares of its decimal digits. 1 is already happy. 7 reaches 1 in 5 steps. 4 is unhappy and the repeat is 4. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
Whether n is a base-10 Harshad number: n is divisible by the sum of its decimal digits. 18 is Harshad, and 11 is not. n runs from 1 to 999999999999999.

Whether n is a Harshad number in base b: n is divisible by the sum of its base-b digits. 10 is Harshad in base 2. 13 is not Harshad in base 10. n runs from 1 to 999999999999999, and b runs from 2 to 36.

Additive persistence: how many times the decimal digits of n must be summed to reach a single digit, and that digit. 199 takes 3 steps and ends at 1. A single digit takes 0 steps. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.

Multiplicative persistence: how many times the decimal digits of n must be multiplied to reach a single digit, and that digit. 39 takes 3 steps and ends at 4. 10 ends at 0 in 1 step. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.

The nth Wedderburn-Etherington number. a(1) is 1, and a(1) through a(6) are 1, 1, 1, 2, 3, 6. Even and odd indices use the binary-tree split, with the middle term only on an even index. n runs from 1 to 80. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The sum of Wedderburn-Etherington numbers from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from a(1) through a(6) is 14. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 1 to 80. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
a(n) mod m for the Wedderburn-Etherington numbers. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 1 to 80. The residue is smaller than the modulus.

The smallest index n with Wedderburn-Etherington number a(n) equal to value. 1 is index 1, and 6 is index 6. A number that is not a term, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 600 digits.

The Wedderburn-Etherington split of n. cross is the sum of a(i)*a(n-i) over the pairs below the middle, and middle is a(k)*(a(k)+1)/2 when n = 2k and 0 when n is odd. n = 6 gives cross 5, middle 1, and value 6. n runs from 1 to 80.
The alternating factorial af(n) = n! - (n-1)! + (n-2)! - ... ending at 1. af(1) is 1, af(3) is 5, and af(4) is 19. n runs from 1 to 200. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The sum of alternating factorials from lo through hi inclusive. The sum from af(1) through af(5) is 127. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 1 to 200. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The Kurepa function K(n), the sum of k! for k from 0 through n-1. K(1) is 1, K(2) is 2, and K(5) is 34. This is the left factorial, not the subfactorial. n runs from 1 to 200. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The superfactorial sf(n), the product of k! for k from 1 through n. sf(1) is 1, sf(3) is 12, and sf(4) is 288. n runs from 1 to 20. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
K(n) mod m for the Kurepa function, the sum of k! from 0 through n-1. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 1 to 200. The residue is smaller than the modulus.
The least prime greater than or equal to n. 0, 1, and 2 all give 2. 14 gives 17. 10000000 gives 10000019. n runs from 0 to 10000000.
The greatest prime less than or equal to n. 2 gives 2, 10 gives 7, and 10000000 gives 9999991. n runs from 2 to 10000000.
pi(n), the number of primes less than or equal to n. pi(0) and pi(1) are 0, pi(10) is 4, pi(100) is 25, and pi(10000000) is 664579. n runs from 0 to 10000000.
The kth prime. The 1st is 2, the 10th is 29, the 100th is 541, and the 664579th is 9999991. k runs from 1 to 664579.
The prime at or below n, the next prime after that one, and the difference. At 10 the prime is 7, the next is 11, and the gap is 4. At 11 the gap from 11 to 13 is 2. n runs from 2 to 10000000.
The number of 1 bits in n. 0 has none, 255 has 8, and 256 has 1. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
The bit length of n: 0 for 0, and one more than the position of the highest 1 bit otherwise. 1 has length 1, 255 has length 8, and 256 has length 9. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
Reverse the lowest width bits of n. 13 reversed in width 4 is 11. 1 reversed in width 8 is 128. n must be smaller than 2^width. width runs from 1 to 62, and n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
The Hamming distance of a and b: how many bit positions differ. 13 and 7 differ in 2 places. 0 and 0 differ in none. Both run from 0 to 999999999999999.
Whether every 1 bit of a is also a 1 bit of b. 3 is a bit-subset of 7. 3 is not a bit-subset of 5. 0 is a bit-subset of 0. Both run from 0 to 999999999999999.
The Kronecker symbol (a/n) for any integers a and n. (2/7) is 1, (3/7) is -1, (2/4) is 0, and (1/0) is 1. Both a and n run from -1000000000000 to 1000000000000.
The Legendre symbol (a/p) for an odd prime p. (2/7) is 1, (3/7) is -1, and (-1/5) is 1. p must be an odd prime. a runs from -1000000000000 to 1000000000000, and p runs from 0 to 1000000000000.
Whether a is a square modulo an odd prime p, counting 0 as a square. 2 is a square mod 7, and 3 is not. -1 is a square mod 5 and not mod 7. p must be an odd prime.
The p-adic valuation v_p(n): how many times the prime p divides n. v_2(12) is 2, v_3(12) is 1, and v_5(12) is 0. p must be prime. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The p-adic valuation of n!, the exponent of the prime p in n!. v_2(10!) is 8, v_3(10!) is 4, and v_2(100!) is 97. p must be prime. n runs from 0 to 1000000000000.
The multiplicative order of a modulo n: the least positive k with a^k = 1 mod n. The order of 2 mod 7 is 3, and the order of 3 mod 7 is 6. a must be coprime to n. n runs from 2 to 1000000.
Whether g is a primitive root modulo the prime p. 3 is a primitive root mod 7, and 2 is not. 1 is a primitive root mod 2. p must be prime and runs from 2 to 1000000.
The least primitive root modulo the prime p. It is 1 for 2, 3 for 7, 5 for 23, and 6 for 41. p must be prime and runs from 2 to 1000000.

The inverse of a modulo m, the residue from 0 to m-1 with a*inverse = 1 mod m. The inverse of 3 mod 7 is 5, and the inverse of -1 mod 7 is 6. There is no inverse when a and m share a factor. m runs from 2 to 1000000000000.

a to the power e, reduced modulo m. 2^10 mod 1000 is 24, 3^5 mod 7 is 5, and (-2)^3 mod 7 is 6. A zero exponent gives 1, including 0^0, except modulo 1 where every power is 0. e runs from 0 to 1000000000000, and m runs from 1 to 1000000000000.

The Eulerian number A(n, k), the number of permutations of n with k ascents. A(4, 1) is 11, A(5, 2) is 66, and A(n, 0) is 1. k runs from 0 through n-1. n runs from 1 to 60. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The Eulerian row A(n, 0) through A(n, n-1), comma-separated. The row for 5 is 1,26,66,26,1. It is symmetric and sums to n!. n runs from 1 to 12.
The sum of Eulerian numbers A(n, k) for k from lo through hi. The whole row sums to n!. A(4, 0) through A(4, 1) is 12. lo must not pass hi, and hi must be an ascent of n. n runs from 1 to 60.
A(n, k) mod m for the Eulerian numbers. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. k must be an ascent of n. n runs from 1 to 60. The residue is smaller than the modulus.
The Eulerian polynomial A_n(x) = sum A(n, k) * x^k. A_3(2) is 13, A_4(1) is 24, and A_5(0) is 1. n runs from 1 to 20, and x runs from 0 to 10. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth central binomial coefficient (2n)!/(n!)^2. C(0) is 1, C(1) is 2, C(5) is 252, and C(10) is 184756. n runs from 0 to 200. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of central binomial coefficients from lo through hi. The sum from C(0) through C(5) is 351. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 200. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
C(n) mod m for the central binomial coefficients. C(10) mod 7 is 5. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 200.

The index n with central binomial coefficient C(n) equal to value. 1 is index 0, and 2 is index 1. A number that is not a term, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 600 digits.
The ratio C(n)/C(n-1) = (4n-2)/n in lowest terms. For 1 it is 2/1, for 2 it is 3/1, and for 3 it is 10/3. n runs from 1 to 200.
Whether n is practical: every integer from 1 to n is a sum of distinct divisors of n. 1, 2, 6, and 12 are practical. 3 and 10 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
How many practical numbers are from 1 through n. There are 5 through 10, and 15 through 40. n runs from 1 to 5000.
Whether some subset of the proper divisors of n sums to n. 6 and 12 are semiperfect. 10 and 70 are not. n runs from 1 to 20000.
Whether n is weird: abundant, but not semiperfect. 70 is weird, and so is 836. 12 is abundant but semiperfect, so it is not weird. n runs from 1 to 20000.

Whether n is amicable, and its partner when it is. The partner of 220 is 284, and the partner of 284 is 220. A perfect number such as 6 is not amicable, and then the partner is 0. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Landau's function g(n), the largest least common multiple of the parts of a partition of n. g(0) is 1, g(5) is 6, g(7) is 12, and g(10) is 30. n runs from 0 to 25.
The sum of Landau's function from lo through hi. The sum from g(0) through g(10) is 100. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 25.
g(n) mod m for Landau's function. g(12) mod 7 is 4, and g(25) mod 97 is 96. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 25.
The smallest n with Landau value g(n) equal to value. 1 is index 0, and 6 is index 5. A number that is not a value, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 12 digits.
The least common multiple of the integers from lo through hi. The LCM of 1 through 10 is 2520, and the LCM of 1 through 11 is 27720. lo must not pass hi. Each end runs from 1 to 40.
Whether n is a lucky number. The list begins 1, 3, 7, 9, 13, 15, 21. 5 and every even number are not lucky. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The kth lucky number. The 1st is 1, the 10th is 33, and the 20th is 79. k runs from 1 to 8772, which is the count of lucky numbers through 100000.
How many lucky numbers are from 1 through n. There is 1 through 1, 2 through 3, and 13 through 50. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The least lucky number greater than or equal to n. 2 gives 3, 20 gives 21, and 49 gives 49. n runs from 1 to 99987, the last lucky number through 100000.
Whether n and n+2 are both lucky. 1, 7, and 13 start a lucky pair. 3 does not, because 5 is not lucky. n runs from 1 to 99985.
The nth hexanacci number. H(0) through H(4) are 0, H(5) is 1, and H(10) is 16. Each later term adds the previous six. n runs from 0 to 512. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of hexanacci numbers from lo through hi. The sum from H(0) through H(10) is 32. lo must not pass hi. Each index runs from 0 to 512. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
H(n) mod m for the hexanacci numbers. H(10) mod 7 is 2, and H(57) mod 97 is 61. The modulus is a positive decimal integer, and zero is rejected. n runs from 0 to 512.

The smallest index n with hexanacci number H(n) equal to value. 0 is index 0, and 1 is index 5. A number that is not a term, or a leading zero, is rejected. value is a decimal integer of at most 600 digits.

The hexanacci step H(n) = H(n-1) + H(n-2) + H(n-3) + H(n-4) + H(n-5) + H(n-6). a through f are those six earlier terms, from oldest to newest. n runs from 6 to 512. Past 15 digits a term is a decimal string.
The largest prime factor of n. It is 1 for 1, 3 for 12, 5 for 30, and 7 for 35. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The smallest prime factor of n. It is 1 for 1, 2 for 12, 5 for 35, and 7 for 49. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n is y-smooth: its largest prime factor is at most y. 12 is 3-smooth and not 2-smooth. 1 is 1-smooth. n and y run from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n is y-rough: its smallest prime factor is at least y. 35 is 5-rough and not 7-rough. 1 is 1-rough and not 2-rough. n and y run from 1 to 1000000000000.

Whether n is y-power-smooth: every maximal prime-power factor p^k is at most y. 12 is 4-power-smooth and not 3-power-smooth. 8 is 8-power-smooth and not 4-power-smooth. n and y run from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n is highly composite: it has strictly more divisors than every smaller positive integer. 1, 2, 6, 12, 60, and 5040 are. 3 and 30 are not. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The least highly composite number greater than or equal to n. 1 gives 1, 3 gives 4, 7 gives 12, and 5041 gives 7560. n runs from 1 to 7560.
How many highly composite numbers are from 1 through n. There are 4 through 10, 9 through 60, and 10 through 120. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The largest number of divisors attained by any integer from 1 through n, and the smallest integer that attains it. Through 10 the record is 4 at 6. Through 12 it is 6 at 12. n runs from 1 to 20000.
Whether n is refactorable: the number of positive divisors of n divides n. 1, 2, 8, 9, and 12 are refactorable. 4 and 6 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.

The Grundy value of a heap of n in the subtraction game with the given move sizes. With moves 1, 2, and 3, the value of n is n mod 4. n runs from 0 to 500, and there are 1 to 8 moves, each from 1 to 100.
Whether the player to move wins a subtraction game on a heap of n with perfect play. A win is a nonzero Grundy value. With moves 1, 2, and 3, 5 is a win and 4 is a loss. n runs from 0 to 500.
Grundy values from heap 0 through heap n in a subtraction game, comma-separated. With moves 1, 2, and 3, the row through 8 is 0,1,2,3,0,1,2,3,0. n runs from 0 to 32.
The nim-sum of a and b, their bitwise exclusive or. 13 xor 7 is 10, and 255 xor 256 is 511. Both run from 0 to 999999999999999.
The mex of a list: the smallest missing nonnegative integer. The mex of 0, 1, 3 is 2. The mex of 1, 2, 3 is 0. The mex of an empty list is 0. The list has at most 64 integers, each from 0 to 1000.
The number of trees on n labeled vertices, n^(n-2). One vertex gives 1, two give 1, three give 3, and four give 16. n runs from 1 to 30. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The number of rooted trees on n labeled vertices, n^(n-1). Four vertices give 64. n runs from 1 to 30. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The Prüfer code of a tree on vertices 1..n. Edges are a flat list of pairs. The path 1-2-3-4 gives 2,3. The star with center 1 and leaves 2,3,4 gives 1,1. Two vertices give an empty code. Vertices run from 1 to 30.
The tree edges for a Prüfer code, as a flat list of sorted pairs. Code 2,3 is the path 1-2-3-4. Code 1,1 is the star at 1. An empty code is the edge 1-2. Code entries run from 1 to 30.

The degree of a vertex in the tree described by a Prüfer code. Degree is one plus the number of times the vertex appears. In code 2,3, vertex 2 has degree 2 and vertex 1 has degree 1. The vertex must lie from 1 to n.

The nth s-gonal number, n*((s-2)*n - (s-4))/2. Triangular 4 is 10, square 5 is 25, pentagonal 5 is 35, and hexagonal 5 is 45. s runs from 3 to 20 and n from 0 to 1000000. The 0th number is 0 and the 1st is 1.

The index n of an s-gonal number. Triangular 10 is index 4, and square 25 is index 5. 0 is index 0. A value that is not s-gonal is rejected. s runs from 3 to 20 and the value from 0 to 999999999999999.
The nth centered s-gonal number, s*n*(n-1)/2 + 1. Centered triangular 4 is 19, centered square 2 is 5, and centered hexagonal 3 is 19. s runs from 3 to 20 and n from 1 to 1000000.
The nth pronic number, n*(n+1). The 0th is 0, the 1st is 2, and the 5th is 30. n runs from 0 to 10000000.
The nth star number, 6*n*(n-1) + 1. The 1st is 1, the 2nd is 13, and the 5th is 121. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether n and n+2 are both prime. 3 pairs with 5, 5 pairs with 7, and 7 does not pair with 9. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000. The partner is n+2.
Whether n and n+4 are both prime. 3 pairs with 7, and 7 pairs with 11. 5 does not pair with 9. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000. The partner is n+4.
Whether n and n+6 are both prime. 5 pairs with 11, 7 pairs with 13, and 3 does not pair with 9. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000. The partner is n+6.
Whether n and 2*n+1 are both prime. 2 gives the safeprime 5, 11 gives 23, and 7 gives 15, which is not prime. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n and (n-1)/2 are both prime. 5 comes from 2, 7 comes from 3, and 23 comes from 11. 3 and 17 are not safeprimes. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The Goldbach split of an even n with the smallest prime p, so n = p+q and p <= q. 10 gives 3 and 7. 20 gives 3 and 17. 4 gives 2 and 2. n is even, from 4 to 10000.
How many Goldbach splits an even n has, with p <= q. 10 has 2, 20 has 2, and 100 has 6. n is even, from 4 to 10000.
Whether p and n-p are both prime. For n=10, p=3 and p=5 work, and p=2 does not. n is even, from 4 to 10000, and p runs from 2 to 10000.
Levy writes an odd n as p+2q with p and q prime, choosing the smallest p. 7 is 3+2*2, 27 is 5+2*11, and 21 is 7+2*7. n is odd, from 7 to 9999.
The lexicographically smallest triple of primes adding to an odd n. 7 is 2+2+3, 9 is 2+2+5, and 27 is 2+2+23. n is odd, from 7 to 9999.

Whether n is a Kaprekar number. Split n^2 so the right part has as many digits as n; the two parts add to n, and the right part is not 0. 1, 9, 45, 297, and 9999 are. 10 is not. n runs from 1 to 10000.
Whether n^2 ends with n. 1, 5, 6, 25, 76, 376, 625, and 9376 do. 10 does not. n runs from 1 to 10000.
Whether n^3 ends with n. 1, 4, 5, 6, 9, 25, 49, 76, 125, and 999 do. 10 does not. n runs from 1 to 10000.
Whether n equals the sum of its digits each raised to the number of digits. 153, 370, 371, and 407 do, and so does every one-digit number. 10 does not. n runs from 1 to 100000.
Whether n is a perfect cube and its digits add to the cube root. 1, 512, 4913, 5832, 17576, and 19683 are. 100 is not a cube. n runs from 1 to 200000. The root is 0 when n is not a Dudeney number.
Whether n equals the sum of the factorials of its digits. 1, 2, 145, and 40585 do. 24 and 10 do not. n runs from 1 to 100000.
Whether n is a composite Smith number: its digit sum equals the digit sum of its prime factors with multiplicity. 4, 22, 27, and 121 are. 6 and every prime are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether n is a composite hoax number: its digit sum equals the digit sum of its distinct prime factors. 22, 58, and 84 are. 4 is Smith but not hoax. Primes are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether n is a product of three distinct primes. 30, 42, 66, and 70 are. 12 and 60 are not, because of the square factor. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether sigma(n) = 2*n - 1. Powers of two, including 1, are almost perfect. 16 gives sigma 31. 6 and 10 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The Mersenne number 2^n - 1. Exponent 1 gives 1, 2 gives 3, and 31 gives 2147483647. n runs from 1 to 128. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Whether 2^n - 1 is prime. Exponents 2, 3, 5, 7, 13, 17, 19, and 31 are, inside this cap. Exponent 11 is not, because 2047 = 23*89. n runs from 2 to 31. This checks the given exponent.
The Fermat number 2^(2^n) + 1. n=0 gives 3, n=4 gives 65537, and n=5 gives 4294967297. n runs from 0 to 12. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Whether the Fermat number 2^(2^n) + 1 is prime. n from 0 through 4 gives a prime. n=5 does not: 4294967297 = 641*6700417. n runs from 0 to 5. This checks the given n.
The Proth number k*2^n + 1. k must be odd and strictly less than 2^n. 1*2^1+1 is 3, and 3*2^5+1 is 97. An even k, or a k that is not below 2^n, is rejected. n runs from 1 to 40.
The Wilson quotient ((p-1)! + 1) / p for a prime p. The quotient of 5 is 5, of 7 is 103, and of 13 is 36846277. A composite is rejected. p runs from 2 to 100. This checks the given prime.
Whether p^2 divides (p-1)! + 1. Inside this cap, 5 and 13 do, and 2, 3, 7, 11, and 17 do not. A composite is rejected. p runs from 2 to 100. This checks the given prime.
Whether n! + 1 and n! - 1 are prime. Both are prime for n=3. For n=11, only n! + 1 is prime. For n=12, only n! - 1 is prime. n! - 1 is not prime for n=0 or 1. n runs from 0 to 12.
Whether n# + 1 and n# - 1 are prime, where n# is the product of the primes up to n. 5# is 30, and both neighbors are prime. 7# is 210, and only 211 is prime. n runs from 2 to 30.
Whether n! + 1 is a perfect square. 4! + 1 = 5^2, 5! + 1 = 11^2, and 7! + 1 = 71^2. The root is 0 when it is not a square. n runs from 1 to 12.
The sum of the first n squares, n*(n+1)*(2n+1)/6. The sum through 1 is 1, and through 10 is 385. n runs from 0 to 1000000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of the first n cubes, (n*(n+1)/2)^2. The sum through 2 is 9, and through 10 is 3025. n runs from 0 to 100000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth tetrahedral number, n*(n+1)*(n+2)/6. The 5th is 35 and the 8th is 120. n runs from 0 to 1000000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The lazy caterer number, the most pieces of a pancake cut by n straight cuts: n*(n+1)/2 + 1. Zero cuts give 1, three give 7, and five give 16. n runs from 0 to 10000000.
The cake number, the most pieces of space cut by n planes: (n^3 + 5*n + 6)/6. Zero planes give 1, three give 8, and five give 26. n runs from 0 to 100000.
The nth Cullen number, n*2^n + 1. The 1st is 3, the 2nd is 9, and the 5th is 161. n runs from 1 to 256. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth Woodall number, n*2^n - 1. The 1st is 1, the 2nd is 7, and the 3rd is 23. n runs from 1 to 256. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth Thabit number, 3*2^n - 1. n=0 gives 2, n=1 gives 5, and n=2 gives 11. n runs from 0 to 256. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth Carol number, (2^n - 1)^2 - 2. n=1 gives -1, n=2 gives 7, and n=3 gives 47. n runs from 1 to 128. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The nth Kynea number, (2^n + 1)^2 - 2. n=1 gives 7, n=2 gives 23, and n=3 gives 79. n runs from 1 to 128. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Whether n = 1 + k*(sigma(n) - n - 1) for a positive integer k, and that k. 6 and 28 give k=1. 21 gives k=2. 12 and 120 do not. k is 0 when n is not hyperperfect. n runs from 1 to 100000.
Whether sigma(n) is a multiple of n, with multiplicity k at least 2. 6 and 28 give k=2. 120 and 672 give k=3. 1 and 12 do not. k is 0 when n is not multiperfect. n runs from 1 to 100000.
Whether sigma(n) = 3*n. 120 and 672 are triperfect. 6 and 28 are perfect, so they are not. n runs from 1 to 100000.

Whether n and m are betrothed: the sum of proper divisors of n is m+1, and the sum for m is n+1, with m different from n. 48 pairs with 75, and 140 pairs with 195. The partner is 0 when n is not betrothed. n runs from 1 to 100000.

Whether n is an Ore number: n times the divisor count is divisible by sigma(n), so the harmonic mean of the divisors is an integer. 1 gives 1, 6 gives 2, and 140 gives 5. 10 does not. The mean is 0 when n is not an Ore number. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The Leyland number x^y + y^x. 2 and 2 give 8, 2 and 3 give 17, and 3 and 3 give 54. x and y each run from 2 to 20. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The Wagstaff number (2^p + 1)/3 for an odd prime p. p=3 gives 3, p=5 gives 11, and p=7 gives 43. An even number or a composite is rejected. p runs from 3 to 127.
Whether the Wagstaff number (2^p + 1)/3 is prime. p=3, 5, 7, and 31 are. p=29 is not. An even number or a composite is rejected. p runs from 3 to 31. This checks the given prime.
Whether n is polite: it is a sum of two or more consecutive positive integers. Every number that is not a power of two is polite. 3, 6, and 9 are. 1, 2, 4, and 8 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.

The shortest sum of consecutive positive integers equal to n. 9 is 4+5, so it starts at 4 and has length 2. 6 is 1+2+3. 100 starts at 18 and has length 5. A power of two is rejected. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The sum of Euler totients from 1 through n. Through 1 it is 1, through 5 it is 10, and through 10 it is 32. n runs from 1 to 100000.

How many reduced fractions lie in the Farey sequence of order n, from 0/1 through 1/1. Order 1 has 2, order 5 has 11, and order 6 has 13. The count is one more than the totient sum. n runs from 1 to 100000.
How many lattice points (x, y) with 1 <= x,y <= n are visible from the origin, meaning gcd(x, y) = 1. The 1-square has 1, the 2-square has 3, and the 5-square has 19. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The sum of gcd(x, y) over 1 <= x,y <= n. Through 1 it is 1, through 5 it is 37, and through 10 it is 189. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The cototient n - totient(n): how many integers from 1 to n share a factor with n. 1 gives 0, 6 gives 4, 9 gives 3, and 10 gives 6. n runs from 1 to 100000.

The surviving seat in the Josephus circle. Seats are 1 through n, counting starts at 1, and every k-th remaining person leaves. 5 people and every 2nd leave seat 3. 41 people and every 3rd leave seat 31. n and k run from 1 to 10000.
The Josephus survivor when every 2nd person is eliminated. Write n = 2^m + l with l < 2^m. The survivor is 2*l + 1. 5 gives 3, 10 gives 5, and 41 gives 19. n runs from 1 to 1000000.

The first person eliminated in the Josephus circle. With 5 people and every 2nd, person 2 leaves first. With every 3rd, person 3 leaves first. A circle of one person has nobody to eliminate. n runs from 2 to 10000 and k from 1 to 10000.
The elimination order in the Josephus circle, comma-separated, not including the survivor. With 5 people and every 2nd, the order is 2,4,1,5. n runs from 2 to 24 and k from 1 to 100.

When a seat is eliminated. Place 1 is the first person out. The survivor has place n. With 5 people and every 2nd, seat 2 has place 1 and seat 3 has place 5. The seat must be from 1 to n. n runs from 1 to 10000.

The sum of the first n fourth powers, n(n+1)(2n+1)(3n^2+3n-1)/30. The sum through 0 is 0, through 1 is 1, and through 10 is 25333. n runs from 0 to 10000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of the first n fifth powers, n^2(n+1)^2(2n^2+2n-1)/12. The sum through 10 is 220825. n runs from 0 to 10000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of the first n sixth powers, n(n+1)(2n+1)(3n^4+6n^3-3n+1)/42. The sum through 10 is 1978405. n runs from 0 to 10000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
The sum of the first n seventh powers, n^2(n+1)^2(3n^4+6n^3-n^2-4n+2)/24. The sum through 10 is 18080425. n runs from 0 to 10000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The sum of the first n odd squares: 1^2 + 3^2 + ... + (2n-1)^2 = n(4n^2-1)/3. One term is 1, two terms are 10, and four terms are 84. n runs from 0 to 1000000. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.

The cyclotomic value Phi_n(a) for an integer a at least 2. Phi_1(2) is 1, Phi_5(2) is 31, Phi_6(3) is 7, and Phi_1(5) is 4. n runs from 1 to 40 and a from 2 to 20. Past 15 digits the value is a decimal string.
Phi_n(1). It is 0 when n is 1. When n is a power of a prime p, it is p. Otherwise it is 1. Phi_4(1) is 2, Phi_6(1) is 1, and Phi_9(1) is 3. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Phi_n(-1). n=1 gives -2, n=2 gives 0, n=6 gives 3, and n=10 gives 5. n runs from 1 to 120.
The coefficient of x^k in Phi_n. Phi_6 has coefficients 1, -1, 1, so k=1 is -1. The coefficient of x^7 in Phi_105 is -2. k past the degree is rejected. n runs from 1 to 120.
The largest absolute coefficient of Phi_n. Phi_1 through Phi_15 have height 1. Phi_105 has height 2. n runs from 1 to 120.
The period of the continued fraction of sqrt(d). sqrt(2) has period 1, sqrt(3) has period 2, sqrt(7) has period 4, and sqrt(13) has period 5. A square is rejected. d runs from 1 to 100000.

The continued fraction of sqrt(d): the integer part a0 and the repeating block, comma-separated. sqrt(2) is 1 with block 2. sqrt(19) is 4 with block 2,1,3,1,2,8. A square is rejected. d runs from 1 to 10000.

Whether x^2 - d*y^2 = -1 has a positive integer solution. It does exactly when the continued-fraction period of sqrt(d) is odd. d=2, 5, and 13 do. d=3, 6, and 7 do not. A square is rejected. d runs from 1 to 100000.
The last term of the repeating block of sqrt(d), which is twice the integer part. sqrt(2) ends in 2, sqrt(3) ends in 2, and sqrt(10) ends in 6. A square is rejected. d runs from 1 to 100000.

How many nonsquares from 1 through n have an odd continued-fraction period, so the negative Pell equation is solvable. Through 2 there is 1, through 10 there are 3, and through 13 there are 4. n runs from 1 to 500.
Whether n is a self number: no m has m plus its digit sum equal to n. 1, 20, and 108 are. 2, 10, and 21 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many self numbers are at most n. Through 1 there is 1, through 10 there are 5, through 20 there are 6, and through 100 there are 13. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The smallest self number that is at least n. 1 stays 1, 2 gives 3, 10 gives 20, and 21 gives 31. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The kth self number. The 1st is 1, the 5th is 9, the 10th is 64, and the 20th is 165. k runs from 1 to 2000.
m plus the sum of its decimal digits. 1 gives 2, 5 gives 10, 19 gives 29, and 99 gives 117. A self number is a number this map never hits. m runs from 0 to 1000000000000.

The factorial-base digits of n, from the highest place down through the 0! place, comma-separated. The last digit is always 0. 0 is "0", 5 is "2,1,0", 23 is "3,2,1,0", and 463 is "3,4,1,0,1,0". n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
The integer value of factorial-base digits. The last entry is the 0! place. [2, 1, 0] is 5 and [3, 2, 1, 0] is 23. A digit in the k! place must be from 0 through k. At most 20 digits.
The digit of the k! place of n. It is floor(n / k!) mod (k+1), and it is 0 when k! exceeds n. The 0! digit is always 0. For 463 the 5! digit is 3 and the 4! digit is 4. k runs from 0 to 20.
How many factorial-base digits n has, including the 0! place. 0 has 1, 5 has 3, 23 has 4, and 24 has 5. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
The sum of the factorial-base digits of n. 0 sums to 0, 5 sums to 3, 23 sums to 6, and 463 sums to 9. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
The number of binary partitions of n, partitions into powers of two. b(0) is 1. Odd n copies b(n-1). Even n is b(n-1) plus b(n/2). b(1) is 1, b(4) is 4, and b(10) is 14. n runs from 0 to 1000.
The sum of the binary partition numbers from b(0) through b(n). Through 0 it is 1, through 4 it is 10, through 10 it is 60, and through 20 it is 390. n runs from 0 to 1000.
The number of plane partitions of n. The values begin 1, 1, 3, 6, 13, 24, so n=5 is 24, n=9 is 282, and n=10 is 500. n runs from 0 to 80.
The sum of the plane partition numbers from 0 through n. Through 0 it is 1, through 2 it is 5, through 4 it is 24, and through 5 it is 48. n runs from 0 to 80.
The number of overpartitions of n. The first part may be overlined. The values begin 1, 2, 4, 8, 14, 24, so n=4 is 14 and n=10 is 232. n runs from 0 to 80.
Whether sigma(n) is strictly larger than sigma(m) for every m below n. 1, 6, 8, and 16 are. 5 and 9 are not. n runs from 1 to 10000.

Whether sigma(n)/n is strictly larger than sigma(m)/m for every m below n. The ratio is compared as sigma(n)*m against sigma(m)*n. 1, 2, 4, 6, and 12 are. 3, 8, and 16 are not. n runs from 1 to 10000.
Whether n is abundant and no proper divisor is abundant. 12, 18, 20, and 70 are. 24 is not, because 12 divides it. 6 is perfect, so it is not. n runs from 1 to 10000.

sigma(n) minus 2n. A perfect number gives 0, an abundant number gives a positive value, and a deficient number gives a negative value. 12 gives 4, 6 gives 0, 10 gives -2, and 1 gives -1. n runs from 1 to 10000.
Whether n equals the sum of its iterated totients down to 1. The sum includes the final 1 and excludes n. 3, 9, 15, and 27 are. 1, 2, and 6 are not. n runs from 1 to 100000.
Whether n is prime and equal to the average of the previous prime and the next prime. 5, 53, 157, and 1103 are. 2, 3, 7, and 11 are not. n runs from 1 to 5000.
Whether n starts a prime triplet: n, n+2, and n+6 are prime, or n, n+4, and n+6 are prime. 5, 7, 11, and 13 do. 3 and 19 do not. n runs from 1 to 10000.
How many prime-triplet starters are at most n. Through 3 there are none, through 5 there is 1, through 13 there are 4, and through 17 there are 5. n runs from 1 to 5000.
Whether n is prime and n+2 is either prime or a product of two primes, counted with multiplicity. 2, 41, and 47 are. 43 is not, because 45 has three prime factors. n runs from 1 to 10000.

Whether odd n is never a prime plus a power of two, counting 2^0. 1 qualifies, because nothing smaller works. 3 is 2+1, so it does not. 127 is the next, and 905 is another. Even n is rejected. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The arithmetic derivative of n. 0 and 1 give 0, a prime gives 1, 4 gives 4, 6 gives 5, 8 gives 12, and 12 gives 16. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The second arithmetic derivative of n. 6 goes 5 then 1. 8 goes 12 then 16. 4 stays 4. 0 and 1 stay 0. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
Whether n equals its arithmetic derivative. 0, 4, 27, and 3125 do. 1, 6, and 16 do not. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The sum of the distinct prime factors of n. 1 gives 0, 8 gives 2, 12 gives 5, and 30 gives 10. A prime gives itself. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether n and n+1 have the same sum of prime factors, counted with repetition. 5, 8, 15, and 714 do. 6 and 9 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether n nuggets can be ordered in boxes of 6, 9, and 20. 0, 6, and 44 can. 1, 11, and 43 cannot. n runs from 0 to 5000.
How many combinations of 6, 9, and 20 boxes add to n. 0 has 1 empty order, 6 has 1, 18 has 2, 43 has 0, and 44 has 2. n runs from 0 to 5000.
The fewest boxes of 6, 9, and 20 that add to n. 0 takes 0, 6 takes 1, 12 takes 2, and 44 takes 4. An amount that cannot be ordered is rejected. n runs from 0 to 5000.
How many integers from 0 through n can be ordered in boxes of 6, 9, and 20. Through 0 there is 1, through 6 there are 2, through 43 there are 22, and through 100 there are 79. n runs from 0 to 5000.
How many positive integers through n cannot be ordered in boxes of 6, 9, and 20. Through 1 there is 1, through 6 there are 5, and from 43 onward there are 22. n runs from 0 to 5000.
How many Collatz steps it takes to reach 1. 1 takes 0, 2 takes 1, 3 takes 7, 6 takes 8, 7 takes 16, and 27 takes 111. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The largest value on the Collatz path from n through 1, including n. 1 peaks at 1, 3 peaks at 16, 7 peaks at 52, and 27 peaks at 9232. n runs from 1 to 100000.
One Collatz step. An even number is halved and an odd number goes to 3n+1. 1 goes to 4, 2 goes to 1, 3 goes to 10, and 6 goes to 3. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many Collatz steps until the value is strictly below the start. 1 is already at the bottom and takes 0. 2 takes 1, 6 takes 1, 3 takes 6, and 7 takes 11. n runs from 1 to 100000.
How many odd terms appear before the Collatz path reaches 1. The final 1 is not counted. 1 and 2 give 0, 3 and 6 give 2, and 7 gives 5. n runs from 1 to 100000.
n divided by its largest square divisor. 12 gives 3, 8 gives 2, 18 gives 2, 36 gives 1, and a square-free n gives itself. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether no cube divides n. 1, 12, 18, and 36 are cubefree. 8, 16, 24, and 72 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether no fourth power divides n. 1, 8, 12, and 36 qualify. 16, 32, 48, and 81 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many square-free positive integers are at most n. Through 1 there is 1, through 4 there are 3, through 10 there are 7, and through 20 there are 13. n runs from 1 to 20000.
How many cubefree positive integers are at most n. Through 7 there are 7, through 8 there are still 7, through 16 there are 14, and through 24 there are 21. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The lower Wythoff number floor(n*phi), phi the golden ratio. n=1 gives 1, n=2 gives 3, n=5 gives 8, and n=10 gives 16. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Which Wythoff sequence contains m, and the index. 1 is lower index 1. 2 is upper index 1. 4 is lower index 3. 5 is upper index 2. m runs from 1 to 1000000.
The sum of the lower Wythoff numbers from index 1 through n. Through 1 it is 1, through 5 it is 22, and through 10 it is 84. n runs from 1 to 100000.
floor(n*sqrt(2)). n=1 gives 1, n=2 gives 2, n=3 gives 4, n=5 gives 7, and n=10 gives 14. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The Beatty complement of sqrt(2), floor(n*(2+sqrt(2))). n=1 gives 3, n=2 gives 6, n=3 gives 10, and n=5 gives 17. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The nth Moser-de Bruijn number, binary digits of n read in base 4. n=0 gives 0, n=3 gives 5, n=5 gives 17, n=6 gives 20, and n=8 gives 64. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The sum of the Moser-de Bruijn numbers a(0) through a(n). Through 0 it is 0, through 3 it is 10, through 5 it is 43, and through 7 it is 84. n runs from 0 to 5000.
Whether every base-4 digit of n is 0 or 1. 0, 1, 4, 5, and 20 qualify. 2 and 6 do not. n runs from 0 to 1000000000000.
The index whose Moser-de Bruijn number is n. 0 is index 0, 5 is index 3, 20 is index 6, and 64 is index 8. A base-4 digit above 1 is rejected. n runs from 0 to 1000000000000.

How many Moser-de Bruijn numbers are at most n, counting 0. Through 0 there is 1, through 1 there are 2, through 5 there are 4, through 16 there are 5, and through 64 there are 9. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
Hofstadter G. G(0) is 0, G(1) and G(2) are 1, G(5) is 3, and G(10) is 6. The rule is G(n) = n - G(G(n-1)). n runs from 0 to 5000.
The sum of Hofstadter G from 0 through n. Through 0 it is 0, through 1 it is 1, through 5 it is 10, and through 10 it is 35. n runs from 0 to 5000.
Hofstadter's female sequence. F(0) and F(1) are 1, F(5) is 3, and F(7) and F(8) are 5. The male term at the same index is computed first. n runs from 0 to 5000.
Hofstadter's male sequence. M(0) and M(1) are 0, M(2) is 1, M(5) is 3, and M(7) is 4. n runs from 0 to 5000.
Conway's Hofstadter sequence. a(1) and a(2) are 1, a(6) is 4, a(10) is 6, and a(16) is 8. The rule is a(n) = a(a(n-1)) + a(n-a(n-1)). n runs from 1 to 5000.
The nth Euclid-Mullin prime. a(1) is 2, a(4) is 43, a(7) is 5, and a(8) is 6221671. n runs from 1 to 8.
The product of the first n Euclid-Mullin primes. n=1 gives 2, n=4 gives 1806, n=7 gives 6221670, and n=8 gives 38709183810570. n runs from 1 to 8.
The sum of the first n Euclid-Mullin primes. Through 1 it is 2, through 4 it is 55, through 7 it is 126, and through 8 it is 6221797. n runs from 1 to 8.
One more than the product of the earlier terms, divided by a(n). It is 1 when that Euclid number is itself prime. n=5 gives 139, n=6 gives 443, n=7 gives 248867, and n=8 gives 1. n runs from 2 to 8.
Where p sits among the first eight Euclid-Mullin primes, or 0 if it does not. 2 is 1, 43 is 4, 5 is 7, and 11 is 0. p runs from 2 to 6221671.
The nth partial quotient of e, starting at n=0. It is 2, then 1, 2, 1, 1, 4, 1, 1, 6. n=0 gives 2, n=5 gives 4, and n=8 gives 6. n runs from 0 to 10000.
The sum of the partial quotients of e from index 0 through n. Through 0 it is 2, through 2 it is 5, through 5 it is 11, and through 8 it is 19. n runs from 0 to 10000.
The partial quotients of e from index 0 through n, comma-separated. Through 0 it is "2". Through 5 it is "2,1,2,1,1,4". Through 8 it is "2,1,2,1,1,4,1,1,6". n runs from 0 to 40.
The nth convergent of e, as numerator and denominator. n=0 is 2/1, n=1 is 3/1, n=2 is 8/3, and n=5 is 87/32. n runs from 0 to 20.
The partial sum of 1/k! from k=0 through n, as a reduced fraction. n=0 is 1/1, n=2 is 5/2, n=3 is 8/3, n=4 is 65/24, and n=5 is 163/60. n runs from 0 to 15.
Whether n is a Keith number. 14, 19, 28, 47, 61, 75, and 197 are. 10, 11, and any one-digit number are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The digit recurrence of a Keith number, comma-separated, through n itself. 14 gives "1,4,5,9,14". A number that is not Keith is rejected. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many new terms are generated after the digits before a Keith number reaches itself. 14 takes 3 and 197 takes 5. A number that is not Keith is rejected. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many Keith numbers are at most n. Through 13 there are none, through 14 there is 1, through 100 there are 6, and through 197 there are 7. n runs from 1 to 10000.
The smallest Keith number that is at least n. 1 and 14 give 14, 15 gives 19, and 76 gives 197. n runs from 1 to 2000.
The fewest positive cubes that add to n. 0 takes 0, 1 takes 1, 8 takes 1, 9 takes 2, 23 takes 9, and 29 takes 3. n runs from 0 to 2000.
How many ways n is a sum of positive cubes, ignoring order and allowing repeats. 0 has 1 empty sum, 2 has 1, 8 has 2, and 16 has 3. n runs from 0 to 2000.
How many ways n is a sum of two positive cubes, ignoring order and allowing the two cubes to be equal. 2 has 1, 9 has 1, 91 has 1, and 1729 has 2. n runs from 0 to 100000.
Whether n has at least two different writings as a sum of two positive cubes. 1729 and 4104 do. 91 and 100 do not. n runs from 0 to 100000.

How many positive integers through n have at least two writings as a sum of two positive cubes. Through 100 there are none, through 1729 there is 1, and through 4104 there are 2. n runs from 0 to 5000.
Whether n reads the same forwards and backwards. 0, 7, and 121 do. 10 and 89 do not. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
n plus its digit reversal. 10 gives 11, 19 gives 110, and 121 gives 242. A trailing zero reverses as a leading zero and does not change the value. n runs from 0 to 10000.
How many reverse-and-add steps turn n into a palindrome. 7 and 121 take 0, 10 takes 1, 19 takes 2, and 89 takes 24. If 50 steps are not enough, the input is rejected. n runs from 0 to 10000.

The palindrome reached by reverse-and-add. 10 reaches 11, 19 reaches 121, and 89 reaches 8813200023188. A palindrome reaches itself. If 50 steps are not enough, the input is rejected. n runs from 0 to 10000.
Whether 50 reverse-and-add steps fail to reach a palindrome. 196 and 295 do. 89, 121, and 10 do not. n runs from 0 to 10000.
One step of the four-digit Kaprekar routine, padding with leading zeros. 3524 gives 3087, 14 gives 4086, 6174 gives 6174, and a repdigit such as 1111 gives 0. n runs from 0 to 9999.
How many steps the four-digit Kaprekar routine takes to reach 6174. 6174 takes 0, 3524 takes 3, 5 takes 6, and 14 takes 7. A repdigit is rejected. n runs from 0 to 9999.
The four-digit Kaprekar chain from n through 6174, comma-separated. 3524 gives "3524,3087,8352,6174" and 6174 gives "6174". A repdigit is rejected. n runs from 0 to 9999.
Whether the four-digit padding of n uses only one digit. 0, 1111, and 2222 do. 5, 111, and 6174 do not. n runs from 0 to 9999.
The value the four-digit Kaprekar routine reaches. Every non-repdigit from 0 to 9999 reaches 6174. A repdigit is rejected. n runs from 0 to 9999.
How many digits the written prime factorization uses, omitting exponents of 1. 1 uses 1, 4 uses 2, 12 uses 3, 16 uses 2, and 125 uses 2. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the written factorization uses fewer digits than n. 125 and 128 do. 1, 16, and 12 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the written factorization uses exactly as many digits as n. 1, 10, 16, and 25 do. 4 and 125 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the written factorization uses more digits than n. 4, 6, and 12 do. 10 and 125 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many frugal numbers are at most n. Through 124 there are none, through 125 there is 1, and through 200 there are 2. n runs from 1 to 10000.
Whether n has no zero digit and the product of its digits divides n. 1, 11, 12, 24, and 36 do. 10, 13, and 22 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many Zuckerman numbers are at most n. Through 9 there are 9, through 12 there are 11, through 24 there are 13, and through 50 there are 14. n runs from 1 to 100000.
Whether every digit of n is nonzero, the digits are all different, and each digit divides n. 12, 15, 24, 124, and 135 do. 10, 11, and 13 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000000.
Whether the first k digits of n form a multiple of k, for every k. 0, 10, 12, 24, 102, and 3816547290 do. 11 and 103 do not. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
How many polydivisible numbers from 0 through n there are. Through 1 there are 2, through 10 there are 11, through 12 there are 12, and through 30 there are 21. n runs from 0 to 100000.
Whether n is a vampire number. 1260, 1395, 1435, and 6880 are. 1000 and 1261 are not. n runs from 1 to 9999.
The smaller-first fang pair of a vampire number, comma-separated. 1260 gives "21,60" and 6880 gives "80,86". A non-vampire is rejected. n runs from 1 to 9999.
The smaller fang of a vampire number. 1260 gives 21, 1395 gives 15, and 6880 gives 80. A non-vampire is rejected. n runs from 1 to 9999.
How many vampire numbers are at most n. Through 1259 there are none, through 1500 there are 3, through 2187 there are 6, and through 6880 there are 7. n runs from 1 to 9999.
The smallest vampire number that is at least n. 1000 and 1260 give 1260, 1261 gives 1395, and 2188 gives 6880. n runs from 1 to 9999.
The home prime of n. 2 stays 2, 4 becomes 211, 10 becomes 773, and 16 becomes 31636373. The search stops after 20 steps or 12 digits. n runs from 2 to 10000.
How many factor-concatenations turn n into a prime. 2 takes 0, 6 and 12 take 1, 4 takes 2, and 10 and 16 take 4. A chain past 20 steps or 12 digits is rejected. n runs from 2 to 10000.
One concatenation of the prime factors of n, repeats included and primes left unchanged. 2 gives 2, 4 gives 22, 8 gives 222, 9 gives 33, and 10 gives 25. n runs from 2 to 10000.
How many digits the home prime of n has. 2 has 1, 4 and 10 have 3, and 16 has 8. A chain past 20 steps or 12 digits is rejected. n runs from 2 to 10000.
Whether the home prime of n has more digits than n. 4, 6, and 10 do. 2 and 21 do not. A chain past 20 steps or 12 digits is rejected. n runs from 2 to 10000.
The digit in place pos of 123456789101112..., counting from 1. Place 9 is 9, place 10 is 1, place 11 is 0, and place 190 is 1. pos runs from 1 to 999999999999.
Which integer owns place pos in the Champernowne digit stream. Place 10 and 11 belong to 10, place 12 belongs to 11, and place 190 belongs to 100. pos runs from 1 to 999999999999.
Where place pos sits inside its integer, counting from 1 on the left. Place 10 is position 1 of 10, place 11 is position 2, and place 12 is position 1 of 11. pos runs from 1 to 999999999999.
The first Champernowne place occupied by the integer m. 1 starts at 1, 10 starts at 10, 11 starts at 12, and 100 starts at 190. m runs from 1 to 999999999999.
How many digits are used to write the integers from 1 through m. Through 9 there are 9, through 10 there are 11, through 13 there are 17, and through 100 there are 192. m runs from 1 to 999999999999.
The integer complexity of n, the fewest 1s added and multiplied to reach n. 1 is 1, 6 is 5, 12 is 7, and 23 is 11. n runs from 1 to 1000.
The sum of the integer complexities from 1 through n. Through 1 it is 1, through 10 it is 45, and through 12 it is 60. n runs from 1 to 1000.
The largest integer complexity attained from 1 through n. Through 1 it is 1, through 10 it is 7, and through 12 it is 8. n runs from 1 to 1000.
How many integers from 1 through n have the same complexity as n. 5 has 1, 6 has 2, 10 has 1, and 12 has 2. n runs from 1 to 1000.
The smallest positive integer whose complexity is k. k=1 gives 1, k=6 gives 7, k=8 gives 11, k=11 gives 23, and k=12 gives 41. k runs from 1 to 19.
Whether the divisors of n split into two sets with equal sum. 6, 12, 20, and 945 do. 1, 10, and 18 do not. n runs from 1 to 2000.
Half the sum of the divisors of n. 6 gives 6, 10 gives 9, and 12 gives 14. An odd divisor-sum is rejected. n runs from 1 to 2000.

One set of divisors that sums to half the divisor-sum, comma-separated, taking the earliest divisors. 6 gives "1,2,3" and 20 gives "2,4,5,10". An odd sum is rejected, and a missing split is rejected. n runs from 1 to 2000.
How many Zumkeller numbers are at most n. Through 1 there are none, through 6 there is 1, through 12 there are 2, through 20 there are 3, and through 30 there are 6. n runs from 1 to 200.
Whether n is an odd Zumkeller number. 945 is. 1, 9, and 15 are not, and an even Zumkeller number such as 6 is not. n runs from 1 to 2000.

One juggler step. An even n goes to its integer square root, and an odd n goes to the integer square root of its cube. 1 stays 1, 2 gives 1, 3 gives 5, 9 gives 27, and 10 gives 3. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many juggler steps reach 1. 1 takes 0, 2 takes 1, 3 takes 6, 7 takes 4, and 9 takes 7. n runs from 1 to 20.
The largest term on the juggler path from n down to 1. 1 peaks at 1, 3 peaks at 36, and 9 peaks at 140. n runs from 1 to 20.
How many odd terms appear before the final 1 on the juggler path. 1 and 2 have none, 7 has 1, 5 has 2, and 3 and 9 have 3. n runs from 1 to 20.
The juggler path from n through 1, comma-separated. 1 gives "1" and 3 gives "3,5,11,36,6,2,1". n runs from 1 to 20.

Narayana's cow sequence at n, counting from 1. The first three terms are 1, and each later term is the previous term plus the term three back. a(4) is 2, a(6) is 4, a(11) is 28, and a(15) is 129. n runs from 1 to 60.
The sum of the first n Narayana cow numbers. The first term sums to 1, the first 3 sum to 3, the first 6 sum to 12, and the first 11 sum to 87. n runs from 1 to 60.
The smallest Narayana cow number that is at least n. 1 gives 1, 3 gives 3, 5 gives 6, and 130 gives 189. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The first index, counting from 1, where Narayana's cow sequence equals n. 0 means n is not a term. 1 is 1, 2 is 4, 4 is 6, 28 is 11, and 5 is 0. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Narayana's cow term a(n) modulo m. a(11) mod 5 is 3, and a(15) mod 10 is 9. n runs from 1 to 60 and m runs from 1 to 1000000.
The sum of the digits of n each raised to k. 0 to any k from 1 up is 0. 153 to the 3 is 153. 4150 to the 5 is 4150, and 4150 to the 4 is 882. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999 and k runs from 1 to 15.

Whether n equals the sum of its digits each raised to k. 153 with k=3, 1634 with k=4, and 4150 with k=5 do. 4150 with k=4 does not, and neither does 2 with k=3. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999 and k runs from 1 to 15.

How many integers from 0 through n equal the sum of their digits each raised to k. For k=3, through 1 there are 2 and through 407 there are 6. For k=5, through 4150 there are 3 and through 4151 there are 4. n runs from 0 to 20000 and k runs from 1 to 10.
Whether n equals the sum of its digits each raised to itself, taking 0^0 as 1. 1 and 3435 do. 0, 2, and 438579088 do not. n runs from 0 to 9999999999.
The sum of the digits of n each raised to itself, taking 0^0 as 1. 0 gives 1, 1 gives 1, 2 gives 4, 10 gives 2, 3435 gives 3435, and 438579088 gives 438579089. n runs from 0 to 9999999999.
The base -2 digits of n, without a leading zero except for 0 itself. 0 is "0", 1 is "1", 2 is "110", 4 is "100", and 6 is "11010". n runs from 0 to 999999999999.
The integer written by a base -2 bit string. "0" is 0, "110" is 2, "100" is 4, and "11010" is 6. A character other than 0 or 1, or a leading zero, is rejected.

The base -2 digit of n in place, counting from 0 at the right. For 6, which is "11010", place 0 is 0, place 1 is 1, and place 4 is 1. A place past the end is 0. n runs from 0 to 999999999999 and place runs from 0 to 60.
How many digits the base -2 writing of n uses. 0 uses 1, 4 uses 3, and 6 uses 5. n runs from 0 to 999999999999.
How many 1 digits the base -2 writing of n has. 0 has none, 1 has 1, 6 has 3, and 7 has 4. n runs from 0 to 999999999999.
The balanced ternary digits of n. -1 is written as T. 0 is "0", 2 is "1T", 4 is "11", 5 is "1TT", and 6 is "1T0". n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
The integer written by balanced ternary digits, where T means -1. "0" is 0, "T" is -1, "1T" is 2, "10" is 3, and "1TT" is 5. A bad digit or a leading zero is rejected.

The balanced ternary digit of n in place, counting from 0 at the right, as -1, 0, or 1. For 5, which is "1TT", place 0 and place 1 are -1 and place 2 is 1. A place past the end is 0. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999 and place runs from 0 to 40.
How many balanced ternary digits n uses. 0 uses 1, 5 uses 3, and 14 uses 4. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
How many nonzero balanced ternary digits n uses. 0 has none, 3 has 1, 6 has 2, and 5 has 3. n runs from 0 to 999999999999999.
Whether n is a Hamming number, that is 5-smooth. 1, 10, 30, and 36 are. 7 and 14 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The nth Hamming number, counting from 1. The 1st is 1, the 10th is 12, the 18th is 30, and the 20th is 36. n runs from 1 to 400.
How many Hamming numbers are at most n. Through 1 there is 1, through 7 there are 6, through 10 there are 9, through 12 there are 10, and through 30 there are 18. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
The smallest Hamming number that is at least n. 7 gives 8, 10 stays 10, 11 gives 12, and 31 gives 32. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Where n sits in the Hamming sequence, counting from 1, or 0 if it is not Hamming. 1 is 1, 12 is 10, 36 is 20, and 7 is 0. n runs from 1 to 1000000000000.
Whether n divided by its digit sum is a prime. 18, 21, and 27 are. 1, 10, 12, and 24 are not. n runs from 1 to 5000.
n divided by its digit sum, when that division is exact. 18 gives 2, 21 gives 7, 12 gives 4, and 1 gives 1. A digit sum that does not divide n is rejected. n runs from 1 to 5000.
How many Moran numbers are at most n. Through 1 there are none, through 18 there is 1, through 21 there are 2, through 30 there are 3, and through 100 there are 7. n runs from 1 to 2000.
The smallest Moran number that is at least n. 1 and 18 give 18, 19 gives 21, 22 gives 27, and 100 gives 111. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The sum of the Moran numbers that are at most n. Through 1 it is 0, through 18 it is 18, through 21 it is 39, through 30 it is 66, and through 100 it is 300. n runs from 1 to 2000.
The smallest positive k such that n divides k!. 1 gives 1, 6 gives 3, 8 gives 4, 9 gives 6, 12 gives 4, and 16 gives 6. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The sum of S(k) from 1 through n. Through 1 it is 1, through 6 it is 18, through 10 it is 40, and through 12 it is 55. n runs from 1 to 5000.
S(n)! divided by n. 1 gives 1, 6 gives 1, 8 gives 3, 9 gives 80, 10 gives 12, and 16 gives 45. n runs from 1 to 20.
n minus S(n). 1 and 4 give 0, 6 gives 3, 8 gives 4, 10 gives 5, and 16 gives 10. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The smallest positive integer m with S(m) = k. k=1 gives 1, k=6 gives 9, k=8 gives 32, k=9 gives 27, and k=11 gives 11. k runs from 1 to 15.
The alternating factorial a(n) = n! - a(n-1), with a(1) = 1. a(3) is 5, a(4) is 19, a(5) is 101, a(6) is 619, and a(8) is 35899. n runs from 1 to 18.
The sum of the alternating factorials from 1 through n. Through 1 it is 1, through 3 it is 7, through 5 it is 127, through 6 it is 746, and through 8 it is 41066. n runs from 1 to 18.
Whether the alternating factorial a(n) is prime. It is for 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 10. It is not for 1, 2, 9, or 12. n runs from 1 to 12.
