The alternating factorial a(n) modulo m. a(5) mod 10 is 1, a(6) mod 100 is 19, and a(4) mod 5 is 4. n runs from 1 to 18 and m runs from 1 to 1000000.
The smallest m at least n, and at most 12, whose alternating factorial is prime. 1 gives 3, 3 stays 3, and 9 gives 10. If none remains through 12, the input is rejected. n runs from 1 to 12.
Whether the binary expansion of n has no two adjacent 1 bits. 0, 1, 2, 5, 10, and 21 do. 3, 6, and 7 do not. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The smallest fibbinary number that is at least n. 0 stays 0, 3 gives 4, 6 and 7 give 8, 11 gives 16, and 21 stays 21. n runs from 0 to 1000000.

How many fibbinary numbers from 0 through n there are. Through 0 there is 1, through 2 there are 3, through 3 there are 3, through 5 there are 5, through 10 there are 8, and through 21 there are 13. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
The nth fibbinary number, counting from 1, with 0 in position 1. The 1st is 0, the 4th is 4, the 8th is 10, the 10th is 17, and the 15th is 33. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The position of n among the fibbinary numbers, counting from 1, or 0 if n is not fibbinary. 0 is 1, 1 is 2, 5 is 5, 10 is 8, 16 is 9, and 3 is 0. n runs from 0 to 1000000.
Whether the average of the divisors of n is an integer. 1, 3, 6, 15, and 20 are. 2, 4, 8, and 12 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The average of the divisors of n, when that average is an integer. 1 gives 1, 3 gives 2, 6 gives 3, 7 gives 4, 15 gives 6, and 20 gives 7. A non-integer average is rejected. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many arithmetic numbers are at most n. Through 1 there is 1, through 2 there is 1, through 6 there are 4, through 15 there are 9, and through 20 there are 12. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The smallest arithmetic number that is at least n. 1 stays 1, 2 gives 3, 4 gives 5, 8 gives 11, and 13 stays 13. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The sum of the arithmetic numbers that are at most n. Through 1 it is 1, through 6 it is 15, through 15 it is 75, and through 20 it is 131. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The Apery number A(n), the sum of C(n,k)^2 * C(n+k,k)^2 for k from 0 to n. A(0) is 1, A(1) is 5, A(2) is 73, A(3) is 1445, and A(5) is 819005. n runs from 0 to 11.
The sum of the Apery numbers A(0) through A(n). Through 0 it is 1, through 2 it is 79, and through 5 it is 853530. n runs from 0 to 11.
A(n) modulo m. A(1) mod 2 is 1, A(5) mod 10 is 5, and A(8) mod 1000 is 425. n runs from 0 to 11 and m runs from 1 to 1000000.
One summand of the Apery number, C(n,k)^2 * C(n+k,k)^2. The k=1 summand of A(2) is 36 and the k=0 summand is 1. A k past n is 0. n and k run from 0 to 11.
Whether the Apery number A(n) is prime. A(1) and A(2) are prime. A(0), A(3), A(5), and A(8) are not. n runs from 0 to 11.
The Franel number F(n), the sum of C(n,k)^3 for k from 0 to n. F(0) is 1, F(1) is 2, F(2) is 10, F(4) is 346, and F(5) is 2252. n runs from 0 to 16.
The sum of the Franel numbers F(0) through F(n). Through 0 it is 1, through 1 it is 3, through 4 it is 415, and through 6 it is 17851. n runs from 0 to 16.
F(n) modulo m. F(4) mod 7 is 3, F(5) mod 10 is 2, and F(8) mod 100 is 62. n runs from 0 to 16 and m runs from 1 to 1000000.
The greatest common divisor of F(n) and F(n+1). n=0 gives 1, n=1 gives 2, and n=6 gives 16. n runs from 0 to 15.
The middle summand of the Franel number, C(n, floor(n/2))^3. n=0 gives 1, n=2 gives 8, n=4 gives 216, n=5 gives 1000, and n=6 gives 8000. n runs from 0 to 16.
The central trinomial coefficient T(n), the coefficient of x^n in (1+x+x^2)^n. T(0) and T(1) are 1, T(2) is 3, T(4) is 19, T(5) is 51, and T(10) is 8953. n runs from 0 to 30.
The sum of the central trinomial coefficients T(0) through T(n). Through 0 it is 1, through 1 it is 2, through 3 it is 12, and through 5 it is 82. n runs from 0 to 30.
T(n) modulo m. T(5) mod 10 is 1, T(6) mod 100 is 41, and T(4) mod 5 is 4. n runs from 0 to 30 and m runs from 1 to 1000000.
The summand C(n,2k)*C(2k,k) of the central trinomial coefficient. For n=5 the summands are 1, 20, and 30. A k past n/2 is 0. n runs from 0 to 30 and k runs from 0 to 15.
Whether T(n) is prime. T(2), T(3), and T(4) are prime. T(0), T(1), T(5), and T(6) are not. n runs from 0 to 30.
The Domb number D(n), the sum of C(n,k)^2 * C(2k,k) * C(2n-2k,n-k) for k from 0 to n. D(0) is 1, D(1) is 4, D(2) is 28, D(3) is 256, and D(5) is 31504. n runs from 0 to 12.
The sum of the Domb numbers D(0) through D(n). Through 0 it is 1, through 2 it is 33, through 4 it is 3005, and through 5 it is 34509. n runs from 0 to 12.
D(n) modulo m. D(5) mod 100 is 4, D(6) mod 1000 is 136, and D(1) mod 3 is 1. n runs from 0 to 12 and m runs from 1 to 1000000.
The greatest common divisor of D(n) and D(n+1). n=0 gives 1, n=1 gives 4, and n=6 gives 64. n runs from 0 to 11.
One summand of the Domb number, C(n,k)^2 * C(2k,k) * C(2n-2k,n-k). The k=1 summand of D(2) is 16 and the k=0 summand of D(3) is 20. A k past n is 0. n and k run from 0 to 12.
The nth octahedral number, n*(2n^2+1)/3. The first terms are 1, 6, 19, 44, and 85. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The sum of the first n octahedral numbers. Through 1 it is 1, through 3 it is 26, through 6 it is 301, and through 10 it is 2035. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The n with O(n) equal to the input, or 0 when the input is not octahedral. 1 is place 1, 6 is place 2, 19 is place 3, and 2 is absent. The input runs from 0 to 666666666700000.
The smallest octahedral number that is at least n. 1 stays 1, 2 gives 6, 7 gives 19, and 45 gives 85. n runs from 0 to 666666666700000.
The nth octahedral number modulo m. O(4) mod 10 is 4, O(5) mod 7 is 1, and O(6) mod 10 is 6. n runs from 1 to 100000 and m runs from 1 to 1000000.
The greedy Egyptian-fraction denominators of a/b, written comma-separated. 3/7 gives 3,11,231. 5/6 gives 2,3. 1/2 gives 2. The fraction must be proper. a and b run from 1 to 30, with b at least 2.
How many unit fractions the greedy Egyptian expansion of a/b uses. 1/2 uses 1, 5/6 uses 2, 3/7 uses 3, and 8/11 uses 4. The fraction must be proper. a and b run from 1 to 30, with b at least 2.
The first denominator in the greedy Egyptian expansion of a/b. 3/7 starts at 3, 5/6 starts at 2, and 2/3 starts at 2. The fraction must be proper. a and b run from 1 to 30, with b at least 2.
The last denominator in the greedy Egyptian expansion of a/b. 3/7 ends at 231, 8/11 ends at 4070, and 1/2 ends at 2. The fraction must be proper. a and b run from 1 to 30, with b at least 2.
The sum of the denominators in the greedy Egyptian expansion of a/b. 3/7 sums to 245, 5/6 sums to 5, and 8/11 sums to 4114. The fraction must be proper. a and b run from 1 to 30, with b at least 2.
The sum of the exponential divisors of n. 1 gives 1, 8 gives 10, 12 gives 18, 16 gives 22, and 36 gives 72. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many exponential divisors n has. 1 and 6 have 1, 8 and 12 have 2, 16 has 3, and 36 has 4. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The exponential divisors of n, comma-separated and ascending. 8 gives 2,8. 12 gives 6,12. 16 gives 2,4,16. 36 gives 6,12,18,36. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the exponential divisors of n sum to 2n. 36 and 180 do. 6, 12, 16, and 60 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The smallest exponential perfect number that is at least n. 1 gives 36, 37 gives 180, 180 stays 180, and 181 gives 252. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The sum of the infinitary divisors of n. 6 gives 12, 8 gives 15, 16 gives 17, 36 gives 50, and 48 gives 68. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many infinitary divisors n has. 6 and 8 and 12 have 4, 16 has 2, and 24 has 8. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the infinitary divisors of n sum to 2n. 6, 60, and 90 do. 16, 24, 36, and 48 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the infinitary divisors of n sum to more than 2n. 24 and 30 do. 6, 16, 36, and 48 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the infinitary divisors of n sum to less than 2n. 1, 16, 36, and 48 do. 6, 24, and 60 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether n is composite and coprime to its divisor sum. 4, 8, 9, 21, and 25 are. 1, 6, 7, and 15 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The greatest common divisor of n and its divisor sum. 4 gives 1, 6 gives 6, 9 gives 1, and 15 gives 3. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many Duffinian numbers are at most n. Through 1 there are 0, through 4 there is 1, through 9 there are 3, and through 30 there are 7. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The smallest Duffinian number that is at least n. 1 gives 4, 5 gives 8, 10 gives 16, and 22 gives 25. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The sum of the Duffinian numbers that are at most n. Through 4 it is 4, through 9 it is 21, through 20 it is 37, and through 30 it is 110. n runs from 1 to 5000.
Whether n lies on an aliquot cycle of length at least 3. 12496 does. 6, 220, and 25 do not. A chain past 30 steps or past one million is rejected as open. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The length of the aliquot cycle containing n, or 0 when n is not on a cycle. 6 gives 1, 220 gives 2, 12496 gives 5, and 25 gives 0. An open chain is rejected. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The smallest member of the aliquot cycle containing n. 284 gives 220 and 14288 gives 12496. A number that is not on a cycle is rejected. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The sum of the aliquot cycle containing n. 6 gives 6, 220 gives 504, and 12496 gives 71056. A number that is not on a cycle is rejected. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The aliquot cycle containing n, starting at n, comma-separated. 220 gives 220,284. 6 gives 6. 12496 gives 12496,14288,15472,14536,14264. A number off a cycle is rejected. n runs from 1 to 20000.
Whether n is 2^a * 3^b + 1. 2, 4, 10, 19, and 145 are. 1, 8, and 11 are not. n runs from 1 to 999999999999999.
Whether n is a Pierpont prime, a prime of the form 2^a * 3^b + 1. 2, 7, 19, and 109 are. 4, 10, 11, and 145 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many Pierpont primes are at most n. Through 1 there are 0, through 10 there are 4, through 20 there are 7, and through 100 there are 10. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The smallest Pierpont prime that is at least n. 1 gives 2, 8 gives 13, 20 gives 37, and 98 gives 109. n runs from 1 to 100000.
The pair a,b with n = 2^a * 3^b + 1. 2 gives 0,0. 10 gives 0,2. 19 gives 1,2. 145 gives 4,2. A number not of that form is rejected. n runs from 1 to 999999999999999.
Whether the preference list is a parking function. (1,1), (2,1), and (1,2,1) are. (2,2) and (1,3) are not. The list has 1 to 8 entries, each from 1 to 8.

Where each car parks, comma-separated. (1,1) parks at 1,2. (2,1) parks at 2,1. (1,2,1) parks at 1,2,3. A list that is not a parking function is rejected. The list has 1 to 8 entries, each from 1 to 8.
The total of parked spot minus preference. (1,1) shifts by 1. (2,1) shifts by 0. (1,2,1) shifts by 2. A list that is not a parking function is rejected. The list has 1 to 8 entries, each from 1 to 8.
How many cars miss their preferred spot. (1,1) moves 1 car. (2,1) moves none. (1,2,1) moves 1. A list that is not a parking function is rejected. The list has 1 to 8 entries, each from 1 to 8.

The first 1-based place where the sorted preferences exceed the place, or 0 when the list is a parking function. (1,1) gives 0. (2,2) gives 1. (3,3,1) gives 2. The list has 1 to 8 entries, each from 1 to 8.
Whether n is a product of two distinct primes that are both 3 mod 4. 21, 33, and 77 are. 9, 15, 25, 35, and 49 are not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
The two prime factors of a Blum integer, smaller first. 21 gives 3,7. 33 gives 3,11. 77 gives 7,11. A non-Blum integer is rejected. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many Blum integers are at most n. Through 20 there are 0, through 21 there is 1, through 33 there are 2, and through 100 there are 6. n runs from 1 to 5000.
The smallest Blum integer that is at least n. 1 gives 21, 22 gives 33, 34 gives 57, and 78 gives 93. n runs from 1 to 10000.
The sum of the Blum integers that are at most n. Through 21 it is 21, through 33 it is 54, through 77 it is 257, and through 100 it is 350. n runs from 1 to 5000.
Whether n is a Carmichael number: composite, squarefree, and p-1 divides n-1 for every prime p dividing n. 561, 1105, and 1729 are. 1, 91, and 341 are not. n runs from 1 to 20000.
The prime factors of a Carmichael number, ascending and comma-separated. 561 gives 3,11,17. 1105 gives 5,13,17. 1729 gives 7,13,19. A non-Carmichael number is rejected. n runs from 1 to 20000.
How many Carmichael numbers are at most n. Through 560 there are 0, through 561 there is 1, through 1729 there are 3, and through 10000 there are 7. n runs from 1 to 10000.
The smallest Carmichael number that is at least n. 1 gives 561, 562 gives 1105, 2000 gives 2465, and 2822 gives 6601. n runs from 1 to 10000.
The sum of the Carmichael numbers that are at most n. Through 561 it is 561, through 1105 it is 1666, through 1729 it is 3395, and through 8911 it is 24193. n runs from 1 to 10000.

The sum of the bi-unitary divisors of n. For a prime power p^e the exponents run from 0 through e, skipping the middle one when e is even. 6 gives 12, 16 gives 27, 36 gives 50, and 48 gives 108. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
How many bi-unitary divisors n has. 1 has 1, 4 and 9 have 2, 8 has 4, and 16 has 4. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the bi-unitary divisors of n sum to 2n. 6, 60, and 90 do. 16, 24, 36, and 48 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the bi-unitary divisors of n sum to more than 2n. 24 and 48 do. 6, 16, and 36 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether the bi-unitary divisors of n sum to less than 2n. 1, 16, and 36 do. 6, 24, and 48 do not. n runs from 1 to 1000000.
Whether n is a Higgs prime for exponent 2. 2, 13, and 19 are. 4, 9, and 17 are not. n runs from 1 to 2000.
How many Higgs primes for exponent 2 are at most n. Through 1 there are 0, through 16 there are 6, through 19 there are 7, and through 100 there are 19. n runs from 1 to 2000.
The smallest Higgs prime for exponent 2 that is at least n. 1 gives 2, 14 gives 19, 17 gives 19, and 73 gives 79. n runs from 1 to 2000.
The 1-based place of n in the Higgs primes for exponent 2, or 0 when n is absent. 2 is place 1, 19 is place 7, and 17 is absent. n runs from 1 to 2000.
The distance from a Higgs prime to the next one. 2 gives 1, 7 gives 4, 13 gives 6, and 71 gives 8. A number that is not a Higgs prime is rejected. n runs from 1 to 2000.
